## What it does

Round 3's entry ([`muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0011/0013: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, paired timing at all six sizes, two-phase `beats_compiled`, the `max_rows` hand-off, and the ready check that judged each `muse-*` variant on its own pass. Round 4 changes three rules ([ADR 0015](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)): an attempt may also hand off below `min_rows`; a handed-off size is reported `handed off` and is not timed against the compiled reference; and candidates that pass together as `muse-all` are `ready` as a **set**. This entry writes only that delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language apart from the two bounds, `capture`, `gpu_lock`, the chained timing and the G3 range rule are cited to round 3, not re-described. The grader was not run and no GPU work was done for this entry; unit-test and re-grade results below are cited to ADR 0015, not re-measured.

## The exact boundary a round-4 solution must keep

A round-4 attempt is inside the boundary only if all five hold. This is the checklist the builders, the boundary agent and the checker grade against; each line names its source.

1. **Spec validity.** `min_rows` and `max_rows` in `spec.json` are each an integer of at least 1, booleans and floats refused, and `min_rows ≤ max_rows` when both are given — otherwise `build()` raises `ValueError` before any kernel runs and the attempt is a G1 failure ([slots.py:330-335](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:174). For `routing+combine` each part's spec carries its own pair of bounds (brief:176).
2. **Inclusive kernel window.** The attempt's kernels run exactly when `min_rows ≤ rows ≤ max_rows` for the bounds it gives (a missing bound is open on that side), and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile` outside that window; `rows` is the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:338-345](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Row-for-row: `hands_off(rows)` is `rows > max_rows or rows < min_rows` ([slots.py:338-339](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)), and `test_hand_off.py` pins the edges bit-for-bit: 8 and 59 run the kernel, 7 and 60 run the compiled reference, for `min_rows: 8, max_rows: 59` ([test_hand_off.py:69](../../../bench/grader/test_hand_off.py)).
3. **G2 bit-exactness at every size, handed off or not.** G2 runs the attempt's `run()` — hand-off dispatch included — on all 20 layers at 1, 8, 32, 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows and requires bit-for-bit equality with the plain reference, in order for routing (including the tied 4th/5th choice) and elementwise for combine/experts; timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:320-351](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:187-195,175). A handed-off size therefore tests `mx.compile(reference)` against the plain reference through the attempt's own dispatch, which is why the boundary also includes compiled==reference at the six sizes (round-3 entry §2; [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). For experts the window must also sit on the right side of MLX's 60-row kernel switch (`gather_qmm_rhs` from 60 rows, different rounding): a decode-built experts kernel may run only below 60 rows, i.e. `max_rows ≤ 59` ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); round-3 entry §2). Inside the window the reference still changes behaviour once: `ref_experts` sorts the pairs from 16 rows (`inds.size >= 64`, [slots.py:62](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)), so a kernel running at both 8 and 32 rows must match the unsorted and the sorted reference, both on the `gather_qvm` side of 60.
4. **Piece-timing phase rule.** At each timed size the verdict is `faster` with ≥22 wins of 30 paired repeats, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:244-250](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). `judge()` drops `handed off` sizes from their phase: a phase is `faster` only when **every** size the kernels run at is `faster` and at least one such size exists, `slower` when any timed size is `slower`, `handed off` when none is left, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:253-271](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:217-218). One `same` at a timed size blocks the bar; one `slower` anywhere fails it.

24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

182|## How each attempt is judged
183|
184|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
185|
186|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
187|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
188|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
189|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
190|
191|   At every size:
192|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
193|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
194|
195|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
196|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
197|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
198|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
199|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
200|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
201|
202|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
203|
204|   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).
205|
206|   **From round 4, a set:** with more than one candidate, the ready check and G3 also time them all together (`muse-all`). When that passes, the candidates are ready together as a set, even where one fails alone, and G3 judges the set as one submission ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).
207|
208|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
209|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
210|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
211|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same`, `slower`, or `handed off` for a size your spec hands to the compiled reference); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
212|
213|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
214|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
215|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
216|- **Handed off** (from round 4): a size whose inputs your spec hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`, `min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is not timed against it. Its verdict is `handed off`, and your attempt's time there is the compiled reference's.
217|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size it doesn't hand off is, and at least one isn't handed off; `slower` when any size is; `handed off` when all are; and `not slower` otherwise.
218|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.

1|# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.
6|
7|## Hardware limits
8|
9|**Peak bandwidth**:
10|The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
11|_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed
12|
13|**Peak compute**:
14|The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
15|_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)
16|
17|**Achieved bandwidth**:
18|The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
19|_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)
20|
21|**Arithmetic intensity**:
22|Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
23|_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio
24|
25|**Ridge point**:
26|The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.
27|
28|**Roofline**:
29|The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.
30|
31|## Bottlenecks and fixes
32|
33|**Bandwidth-bound**:
34|A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.
35|
36|**Compute-bound**:
37|A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.
38|
39|**Overhead-bound**:
40|A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
41|_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)
42|
43|**Bottleneck**:
44|The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
45|_Avoid_: issue, slowness
46|
47|**Kernel**:
48|One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
49|_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)
50|
51|**Occupancy**:
52|The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
53|_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)
54|
55|**Knock-out**:
56|A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
57|_Avoid_: ablation
58|
59|**Baseline**:
60|The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.
61|
62|**Fix**:
63|One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
64|_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak
65|
66|## Inference
67|
68|**Prefill**:
69|Processing a request's whole prompt through the model before its first token is generated, in chunks of up to the engine's token budget per pass (2,048 tokens here).
70|_Avoid_: prompt phase (say prefill, or prompt processing)
71|
72|**Decode step**:
73|One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.
74|
75|**Decode rows**:
76|The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
77|_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency
78|
79|**Client concurrency**:
80|The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
81|_Avoid_: batch size
82|
83|## Mixture of experts
84|
85|**Expert**:
86|One of the interchangeable feed-forward blocks in a layer; MobileMoE-S has 60 routed experts per layer.
87|
88|**Active experts**:
89|The experts the router picks for one token in one layer (4 for MobileMoE-S).
90|_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts
91|
92|**Distinct experts**:
93|The number of different experts used by all decode rows together in one layer during one decode step; it decides how much expert weight data the step must read.
94|_Avoid_: unique experts, expert coverage

1|# Attempt 2 — builder-1-b, direction (b): FP-contract-off pragma barrier
2|
3|First attempt in this direction (round 3, `hyp-1-combine-devolatilize`,
4|slot `combine`, baseline `none`). Builds on the starting point
5|`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`, which passes G1+G2 and

8|## What changed
9|
10|Only the barrier mechanism. Grid (`rows*768`), threadgroup [256,1,1],
11|index/base lines, inputs/outputs and the final
12|`bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` line are verbatim from the starting
13|point. The seven `volatile float` locals (`p0..p3`, `s01`, `s012`,
14|`acc`) become seven plain `float` locals with the identical 7-op
15|sequence, and a new header block (`block-1.metal`, wired via
16|`"header_block": 1` — the only `spec.json` delta) disables FP
17|contraction for the kernel:
18|
19|```metal
20|#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF
21|#pragma clang fp contract(off)
22|```
23|
24|MLX emits `header` before the main function, so the pragmas precede the
25|kernel definition, which is where FP-option pragmas take effect. No
26|`volatile` anywhere in code, no `__attribute__((noinline))` helpers,
27|no extra functions, calls, or memory traffic of any kind.
28|
29|Why this is contraction-proof: with contract(off) the backend may not
30|fuse any fmul+fadd into an fma — this is the compiler's own
31|contraction switch, so there is no transform left that can keep a
32|product unrounded into its consumer add. Each of the 7 statements is
33|then one rounded f32 op on register values: the same 7 materialisation
34|points, same fold order `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`, same two bfloat16 roundings
35|as the starting point. Reassociation needs no pragma: it is off without
36|fast-math flags, and the grader sets none. The proof is G2 itself: any
37|surviving contraction shows the starting point's old signature (decode
38|0/2/2, prefill 6/50/130 differ).

1|// Header for the devolatilized combine kernel (direction b: compiler
2|// contraction switch, no volatile, no helper calls).
3|//
4|// The Metal compiler FP-contracts mul+add pairs into FMAs by default,
5|// which keeps products unrounded into their consumer add and breaks the
6|// reference's per-op f32 rounding. The two pragmas below switch
7|// contraction off for the kernel function defined after this header
8|// (MLX emits `header` before the main function; `help(mx.fast.
9|// metal_kernel)`). With contraction off, the backend may not fuse any
10|// fmul+fadd into an fma, so each mul and each add in the body rounds
11|// once to f32 with its value living in a register — the same 7
12|// materialisation points as the starting point's seven volatiles, with
13|// zero thread-private memory traffic and no extra instructions.
14|//
15|// Both spellings are given: the standard C99 form and the Clang form.
16|// Either one alone disables contraction for the function; the second is
17|// belt and braces against pragma-dialect drift. They must live here, not
18|// in the body: FP-option pragmas take effect for functions defined after
19|// them, and the body is inside the generated function. Reassociation
20|// needs no pragma: the compiler does not reassociate without fast-math
21|// flags, and the grader passes none (slots.build sets no
22|// compile_options, so math_mode stays "safe").

48|Per layer, at decode 1 / 8 / 32 rows and prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048
49|rows (peak 200 GB/s, `claude/GLOSSARY.md`):

51|- Kernels × fixed cost: 1 kernel/layer either way — the barriers add no
52|  launch; the chained floor (~32–40 µs/layer decode) is shared with the
53|  twin. Not the cost.
54|- Bytes ÷ peak: slot traffic 9,232 B/row plus spill traffic 56
55|  B/thread = rows×43,008 B/layer, i.e. 52,240 B / 418 KB / 1.67 MB at
56|  decode = **0.26 / 2.1 / 8.4 µs**, and 6.6 / 53 / 107 MB at prefill =
57|  **33 / 265 / 533 µs**. Spill bytes alone: 43 KB / 344 KB / 1.375 MB
58|  decode, 5.5 / 43.7 / 88 MB prefill.
59|- Measured (the twin swing, round-2 G3 minus round-1 G3, per decode
60|  step over 20 layers; vLLM medians, plain in brackets):
61|  1 row **+0.142 (+0.433)** ms, 8 rows **+0.508 (+0.641)** ms, 32 rows
62|  **+1.441 (+1.574)** ms — i.e. **+7.1 / +25.4 / +72.1 µs/layer**
63|  (+21.7 / +32.1 / +78.7 plain). Cross-run drift is bounded at ±0.1 ms
64|  by the control both runs timed (round-1 triple within 0.06–0.09 ms;
65|  territory checklist B), so the 8- and 32-row swings are signal; the
66|  1-row swing is within 1-row cross-run noise and claimed as ≈0.
67|  At 32 rows the paid +72.1 µs/layer is ~9× the spill bytes' 8.4 µs
68|  bandwidth time — the cost is stalls on thread-private traffic
69|  (dependent store→load pairs the compiler cannot schedule across,
70|  fetched in cache lines far wider than the 4 B values), not bytes.

73|20-layer link chain runs the kernel against a quiet cache with nothing
74|but the tiny `link` kernel between layers, while the step buries each
75|call between megabytes of neighbouring traffic; the store→load reuse
76|that the quiet chain absorbs on-chip stalls in the busy step. The exact
77|on-chip accounting (L1 absorption, line amplification on strided
78|frames, register pressure) needs GPU counters and is **unverified** —
79|but the attribution does not depend on it: same spec, same grid, same
80|inputs, only delta the barriers, 1.44 ms swing with a ±0.1 ms control.

100|
101|The new rules held:
102|- every end-to-end number in *Ready to test* comes from the ready check, and predictions are labelled;
103|- `checker-final` found 7 rounding slips in the last digit and had them fixed before the round ended;
104|- when the fused experts kernel kept losing at 1 row, attempt-5 changed approach to an unfused path, and its ledger line says so.

107|- **Builders were spent on directions exploration had already ruled out:** experts attempt-2 and routing attempt-3.

109|- **The thread limit cost two attempts.** Metal's limit per pipeline depends on the kernel's registers, 640 and then 576 threads here, while the grader checks only for 1,024. Routing attempts 2 and 4 failed G1 on it.
110|- **The grader timed identical code against itself.** Above `max_rows` an attempt runs the compiled reference, and the grader still timed it against the compiled reference. 44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE

55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )

79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)

283|def dim(expr, rows):

285|        raise ValueError(f"bad size {expr!r}")

304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md);
310|    with "min_rows", so do inputs with fewer rows than that
311|    (claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md). The function's hands_off(rows)
312|    says whether inputs of that many rows run the compiled reference.
313|    """
314|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
315|    kernels = []
316|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
317|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
318|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
319|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
320|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
321|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
322|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
323|            header=header,
324|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
325|        )
326|        kernels.append((k, fn))
327|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
328|    if missing:
329|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
330|    min_rows, max_rows = spec.get("min_rows"), spec.get("max_rows")
331|    for key, v in (("min_rows", min_rows), ("max_rows", max_rows)):
332|        if v is not None and (isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, int) or v < 1):
333|            raise ValueError(f"bad {key} {v!r}")
334|    if min_rows is not None and max_rows is not None and min_rows > max_rows:
335|        raise ValueError(f"min_rows {min_rows} is above max_rows {max_rows}: the kernels would never run")
336|    compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
337|
338|    def hands_off(rows):
339|        return (max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows) or (min_rows is not None and rows < min_rows)
340|
341|    def run(**inputs):
342|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
343|        if hands_off(rows):  # the compiled reference takes over
344|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
345|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
346|        env = dict(inputs)
347|        for k, fn in kernels:
348|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
349|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
350|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
351|            outs = fn(
352|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
353|                template=[
354|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
355|                ],
356|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
357|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
358|                output_shapes=[
359|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
360|                ],
361|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
362|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
363|            )
364|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
365|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
366|
367|    run.hands_off = hands_off
368|    return run

5|# From round 4, candidates that pass together are ready as a set, and an attempt may hand off small inputs too
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Round 3 showed three gaps in the rules ([Claude's measurement](../findings/muse-round-3.md)). On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose to fix all three before round 4:
10|
11|1. **Ready as a set.** Round 3's routing and combine candidates each failed the ready check alone, on overlapping ranges, while the two together (`muse-all`) passed it. The skill made a candidate `ready` only when it passed alone, so the round submitted nothing. From round 4, when `muse-all` passes the ready check, all its candidates are `ready` together as a **set**. A set goes to G3 whole, and G3 judges it as `muse-all`.
12|2. **Hand off below a row count too: `min_rows`.** `max_rows` already sends inputs with more rows to `mx.compile` of the slot's reference ([ADR 0011](0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). The new `min_rows` in an attempt's `spec.json` does the same for inputs with fewer rows, so the kernels run only from `min_rows` to `max_rows`. Round 3's experts attempt-1 lost to the compiled reference only at 1 row: 96.9 against 86.6 µs per layer, while it took 168.9 against 238.2 at 8 rows and 554.7 against 883.4 at 32. Its only way to pass was to win at the size it is worst at.
13|3. **A handed-off size isn't timed.** The grader timed each handed-off size, which runs the compiled reference, against the compiled reference: the same code twice. In round 3 that noise judged routing attempt-1 `slower` at 2,048 rows, on 8 wins of 30, and cost a re-grade of a byte-identical copy. Now such a size is reported `handed off`. A phase is `faster` when every size the kernels run at is faster, and it needs at least one; `beats_compiled` is still one phase `faster` and none `slower`. G2 still checks every size, bit for bit.
14|
15|## How it works
16|
17|- **`bench/grader/slots.py`:**
18|  - `build()` reads `min_rows` as it reads `max_rows`: an integer of at least 1, at most `max_rows` when both are given.
19|  - The function it returns has `hands_off(rows)`, which says whether inputs with that many rows run the compiled reference.
20|- **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:**
21|  - At each size, a function that hands the rows off is not timed. It takes the compiled reference's times, so for `routing+combine` the part that hands off adds the same time to both sides.
22|  - A bar's verdict is `handed off` when neither side ran code of its own. Against a baseline that runs its own kernels there, the size is timed as before.
23|  - `judge()` leaves `handed off` sizes out of a phase. A phase whose sizes are all handed off is `handed off`.
24|- **`bench/grader/test_hand_off.py`:**
25|  - checks `build()` with a toy kernel at row counts on both sides of each bound, bit for bit, and that bad bounds are refused;
26|  - checks `judge()` on five sets of verdicts.
27|  - Passed on 2026-11-04.
28|- **A real attempt.** Claude re-graded round 3's routing attempt-6 (`max_rows` 32) with the changed grader ([results/runs/2026-11-04-grader-hand-off/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-grader-hand-off/)):
29|  - G2 passes;
30|  - decode is `faster` at 1, 8 and 32 rows, on 29, 26 and 27 wins of 30;
31|  - the three prefill sizes are `handed off`;
32|  - `beats_compiled` is true.
33|- **The skill, version 9.**
34|  - The ready check makes a passing `muse-all` a set.
35|  - *Ready to test* names a set's attempts together.
36|  - Builders and boundary agents record `min_rows` and the sizes it hands off.
37|- **G3 and the ready check are unchanged.** They time whole requests, so a slot's kernels count wherever they run. With 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so an attempt that hands off 1 row runs MLX's own code for the whole 1-request workload. Alone it is then no faster than its compiled bar there, and it can pass G3 only in a set whose other kernels are faster with 1 request. The brief says so.
38|
39|## Consequences
40|
41|- **Round 3's pair qualifies for round 4.** Under the set rule, routing attempt-6 with combine attempt-2 would have been `ready` in round 3, because its `muse-all` passed the swarm's ready check. Claude's G3 failed the same pair against the compiled bar at 32 requests of 1,024 tokens, on overlapping ranges, so the pair is still no baseline.
42|- **A set is judged once.** Its parts are not judged alone, so a set can carry a part that only helps together with the others. G3 still requires the whole set to be faster than both bars, and to be slower nowhere.
43|- **The interaction of all three slots is untested.** In rounds 1 and 2, replacing all three slots at once lost about 2.8 ms with 8 requests, for an unknown reason ([round 2](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 4). A set with an experts attempt meets that again.
44|
45|## Considered options
46|
47|- **A paired test on medians for the ready check and G3,** so that one outlier repeat can't sink a candidate, as it sank combine attempt-2 in round 3. Not chosen for round 4: it changes ADR 0011's rule for Claude's G3 too, and there was too little time to check it before the deadline.
48|- **Hand-off by an explicit list of row counts.** More flexible, but no attempt has needed more than one range, and two bounds are simple to check.

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing runs at the same six
9|sizes and chains the 20 layers, so each call waits for the one before, as in
10|the model. The grader prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when
11|given. It writes into an attempt folder only when --out points there, as
12|the Muse agent's builders do with grade.json; load() reads only spec.json and
13|the block-N.metal files.
14|
15|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
16|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
17|
18|The candidate and the compiled reference are timed in alternating repeats, so
19|drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. At each size the candidate is
20|"faster" when it wins at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats (a
21|one-sided sign test at p < 0.01), "slower" when it loses that many, and
22|"same" otherwise; the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
24|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower
25|at none of the other (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
26|
27|A size whose inputs the attempt hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`,
28|`min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is "handed off", not timed against
29|it: a phase is faster when every size the kernels run is, and needs one such
30|size (claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md). G2 still checks it.
31|
32|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run and adds
33|`beats_baseline`, judged the same way. From round 2 on, the bar is the
34|previous round's final attempt for the slot
35|(claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md). FOLDER alone is an attempt
36|for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one routing+combine
37|attempt or `routing=FOLDER` and `combine=FOLDER`.

197|def chained(fn, layers, names):
198|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.

200|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
201|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
202|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
203|    """
204|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
205|    outs = []
206|    for layer in layers:
207|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
208|        if outs:
209|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
210|        out = fn(**args)
211|        if isinstance(out, dict):
212|            out = list(out.values())
213|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
214|    return outs

217|def timed(fn, layers, names):

219|    for _ in range(3):

224|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))

238|            t0 = time.perf_counter()

128|### C. The reference sum's association (`col_reduce_small`, size-4 axis)
129|
130|Per output element (fixed row, fixed column `d`), `reduce_col.h` runs:
131|`totals[i]` (4 column lanes per thread) start at `Sum::init = 0`; the loop
132|over the reduction (`r = lid.y; r < rows·4; r += lsize.y`, `lsize.y = 4`)
133|gives each `lid.y` lane exactly one product, so lane `j` holds
134|`0 + p_j = p_j` exactly; then, if `lsize.y > 1`, the threadgroup fold on
135|`lid.y == 0` computes `t = p_0; t = p_1 + t; t = p_2 + t; t = p_3 + t`,
136|each `op(a,b) = a + b` rounded once to f32. IEEE addition commutes, so the
137|reference association is exactly the left fold **((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃** with a
138|rounding after every add. That association does **not** change with rows:
139|the reduced axis is always size 4; more rows only add threadgroups /
140|non-column reductions. Round 1's boundary emulation already proved the
141|point from the candidate side: all 120 pure association trees of the four
142|products give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches to the grader
143|fingerprint, while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it exactly
144|(`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The 2.0-ULP touch*).

146|### D. The candidate's arithmetic (`block-0.metal:20-25`)
147|
148|The source writes the same left fold, `p₀ + p₁ + p₂ + p₃` as one f32
149|expression, then `bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]`. Compiled as a single
150|Metal kernel (MLX `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, `slots.py:309-316`; no compiler
151|flags are expressible in `spec.json`), the mul+adds are FP-contracted
152|into FMAs: `fma(y_j, w_j, partial)` keeps the product unrounded, so `acc`
153|can differ from the reference fold by ~1 f32 ULP. The bf16 rounding of
154|`acc` absorbs that almost always; it flips only when `acc` lies within
155|the delta of a bf16 rounding midpoint, yielding a 1-ULP-different sum,
156|which the bf16 `+ shared` then preserves — or magnifies in ULP terms
157|when `shared ≈ −sum` cancels toward zero (the grader floors the ULP at
158|`|r| = 0.001`, `check_candidate.py:84-99`, so near-zero results report
159|large ULP gaps from tiny absolute differences). Attempt-2's explicit
160|`acc += product` loop shows the identical fingerprint (0.0 / 2.0 / 1.0),
161|so loop form and staging are exonerated too: only suppressing
162|contraction (e.g. the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary named)

13|## What happens
14|
15|The starting point (`muse-spark/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal:20-25`)
16|writes the 4-term f32 sum as one expression,
17|`float(y0)·w0 + float(y1)·w1 + float(y2)·w2 + float(y3)·w3`, then
18|`bfloat(acc) + shared`. Compiled as a single Metal kernel, the compiler
19|FP-contracts the mul+add pairs into FMAs, keeping each product unrounded
20|into its add. The reference can never do this: `ref_combine`
21|(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`) runs eagerly as separate kernels —
22|`binary_g` multiply (`Multiply` is plain `x * y`, product rounded once
23|to f32), then `col_reduce_small` (`Sum` is plain `a + b`, init 0) folding
24|((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ with a rounding after every add, then `copy_v` bf16
25|round, then `binary_vv` bf16 add (headers under
26|`.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/`;
27|full mapping in `territory-baseline-combine.md` checklist B–D). The
28|candidate's `acc` therefore differs from the reference fold by ~1 f32
29|ULP on some elements; the bf16 rounding absorbs it except when `acc`
30|sits at a rounding midpoint, and the following `+ shared` can magnify
31|the reported gap when it cancels toward zero (ULP floored at
32|`|r| = 0.001`, `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:84-99`).
33|
34|This is contraction, not association: the candidate's written order is
35|already the reference's left fold, and round 1's CPU emulation showed
36|all 120 pure association trees give ≤1.0 ULP at 8 rows with zero matches
37|to the grader fingerprint while the FMA-chain evaluation reproduces it
38|exactly (`muse-spark/implementation/hyp-3-fused-combine.md`, *The
39|2.0-ULP touch*). Attempt-2's explicit `acc += …` loop has the identical
40|fingerprint, so neither loop form nor staging avoids contraction — the
41|fix must suppress it (the `precise` accumulator round 1's boundary
42|named there) while keeping the ((p₀+p₁)+p₂)+p₃ fold and both bf16
43|rounding points.
44|
45|Under round 2's bit-exact G2 (`claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md`)
46|the kernel fails at five of six sizes
47|(`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-1/grade-exact-combine.json`, summed
48|over 20 layers): decode 1 row 0 differ (pass), 8 rows **2** (max
49|2.0 ULP), 32 rows **2** (max 1.0 ULP); prefill 127 rows **6** (1.0),
50|1,016 rows **50** (16.0), 2,048 rows **130** (32.0). The count grows at
51|a roughly constant 3–16 ppm of rows·768·20 elements — the same lottery
52|sampled more times, not a prefill kernel switch (combine's kernels are
53|row-count-invariant; the 60-row experts switch cannot enter through
54|captured `y`). In the model, these differences changed 7 of 32 vLLM

9|## What it does
10|
11|The `experts` slot of one MoE layer: for each row `r` and slot
12|`j`, `y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]`
13|with `e = inds[r, j]`. The code in the slot is round 3's
14|`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/experts/attempt-1`: one fused per-pair
15|kernel (512 threads per pair, `rows*4` threadgroups) plus
16|`"max_rows": 59` in `spec.json`, so rows 1–59 run the fused kernel
17|and rows above 59 run the compiled reference. It passes G2
18|bit-exact at all six sizes, beats compiled at 8/32 decode rows,
19|and loses at 1 row — the only reason `beats_compiled` is false.

21|Round 3's `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md`
22|and `ineff-baseline-experts-1/2.md` (both confirmed, frozen) and
23|`muse-spark/round-3/implementation/hyp-2-experts-prefill.md`
24|(frozen) mapped this code when it was attempt-7 plus the hand-off.
25|This entry cites them where they still hold and writes only what
26|is new for round 4: the `min_rows: 2` spec change ADR 0015 adds,
27|and where the fused kernel still spends its time now that 1 row
28|and prefill can both leave the kernel.
29|
30|## What `min_rows: 2` with `max_rows: 59` changes (new)
31|
32|The grader now supports a lower hand-off bound. `build()` reads
33|`min_rows` like `max_rows` (int ≥ 1, ≤ `max_rows` when both are
34|given, bools rejected) and the returned function hands off when
35|`rows > max_rows or rows < min_rows`
36|(`bench/grader/slots.py:330-343`); the brief states the same
37|contract (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:174`). Adding
38|`"min_rows": 2` to the starting point's `spec.json` — no kernel
39|change — moves the kernel-visible window from 1–59 to **2–59**:

41|- **1 row: handed off.** The kernels no longer run there at all.
42|  G2 still checks the size, but through the attempt's own
43|  dispatch it runs the compiled reference, which was bit-exact
44|  with the reference at all six sizes in round 3

{"path":"muse-spark/round-4/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md","content":"# Territory: baseline-combine

- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-combine
- **Status:** exploring
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T21:44:10Z
- **Next:** post the two inefficiency entries, then set done

## What it does

Each of the 20 layers returns
`out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(bf16) + shared`
(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52`; in the model
`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:230-232`). The code now
in the `combine` slot is round 3's
`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/`: one fused
thread-per-output kernel whose seven `volatile` rounding barriers are
seven plain `float` locals, with FP contraction disabled by a header
pragma pair instead of by memory traffic. It passes G1+G2 bit-exact
and `beats_compiled` at all six sizes, but failed G3 alone on
5-repeat range overlap, so it is a starting point, not a baseline
(`muse-spark/round-4/exploration/README.md` *Starting point*;
`claude/findings/muse-round-3.md` §§1–2). Round 3's
`territory-baseline-combine.md`, `ineff-baseline-combine-1.md` and
`implementation/hyp-1-combine-devolatilize.md` are frozen and cited;
this entry writes only what is new for round 4: whether any
bit-exact change widens the decode margin, what the pragma leaves in
the compiled binary, and the chained-floor costs of this kernel.

## Checklist

### A. Launch spec: `spec.json` (attempt-2)

- **Callers:** `slots.build` turns the spec into one
  `mx.fast.metal_kernel` call (`bench/grader/slots.py:304-326`); the
  grader calls it per layer as `fn(y=…, weights=…, shared=…)`
  (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:152-154,323-347`), and in serving
  it replaces the combine line via `slots.make_moe_call`
  (`bench/grader/slots.py:97-119`, combine at `:116`). Shapes: decode
  1 / 8 / 32 rows, prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows.
- **Callees:** one kernel launch per layer, 20 per step.
  `spec.json` (single line): name `fused_combine`, `source_block` 0,
  `header_block` 1, inputs `y, weights, shared`, output `out`
  [rows,768] bfloat16, grid `rows*768`, threadgroup [256,1,1],
  `template` {}, `init_value` null, `atomic_outputs` false. **No
  `max_rows`, no `min_rows`:** `hands_off(rows)` is therefore false
  at every row count (`bench/grader/slots.py:330-343`), so the
  round-4 `handed off` verdict never applies to this slot and every
  graded size runs this kernel. Adding a hand-off now would only
  surrender a win (see *Decode margin* below).
- **Data:** `y` bf16 [rows,4,768] row-contiguous, `weights` f32
  [rows,4], `shared` bf16 [rows,768] → `out` bf16 [rows,768];
  9,232 B/row unique traffic (6,144 + 16 + 1,536 + 1,536). Frozen
  accounting in round 3's territory checklist A still holds; the
  kernel adds no threadgroup memory, no atomics, no second kernel.
- **Neighbours:** before: experts' `y`, routing's `weights`
  (positional pairing `weights[r,j] ↔ y[r,j,:]`), shared expert's
  `shared` (outside the slots); after: residual add
  `h + feed_forward(…)` (`mobilemoe.py:258`). A replacement must
  keep shapes, dtypes, the f32 fold and both bf16 rounding points.
- **Cost:** measured, piece: `grade.json` — candidate 31.8 / 34.7 /
  32.7 µs/layer decode and 38.2 / 100.9 / 198.0 prefill vs compiled
  36.9 / 41.1 / 45.7 and 64.0 / 281.8 / 556.2 (same-run paired
  verdicts `faster` at all six, 24 / 27 / 30 / 30 / 30 / 29 wins).
  Full floor arithmetic is in section D and
  `ineff-baseline-combine-1`.
- **Invariants:** G2 `differ == 0` at all six sizes (grader compares
  against the eager reference, `check_candidate.py:152-163,351`;
  `mx.compile` appears only in timing). Any change must keep: exact
  bf16→f32 casts; each product rounded once to f32; left fold
  `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3` with a rounding after every add; one bf16 round;
  single-rounding bf16 `+ shared`. Combine has no 60-row kernel
  switch underneath (that switch is the experts slot's).

### B. Kernel body: `block-0.metal` (attempt-2)

- **Callers / Callees:** as in A; the body is the whole kernel
  (`block-0.metal:26-42`). One thread per output element:
  `idx = thread_position_in_grid.x`, `row = idx / 768`,
  `d = idx - row*768` (`:26-28`), then `wbase`, `ybase`, `sbase`
  (`:30-32`).
- **Data / arithmetic:** four products
  `p_j = float(y[ybase + j*768]) * weights[wbase + j]` (`:34-37`),
  fold `s01 = p0+p1`, `s012 = s01+p2`, `acc = s012+p3` (`:38-40`),
  final line verbatim from every predecessor:
  `out[sbase] = bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` (`:42`). Seven f32
  materialisations, no `volatile`, no helper calls, no threadgroup
  memory in this attempt (contrast attempt-1's `noinline` helpers,
  `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-1.metal`).
  Loads: 4 bf16 `y` values strided 768 elements (coalesced within
  each expert plane — consecutive threads read consecutive `d`),
  the same 4 `weights` re-read by all 768 threads of a row
  (L1-broadcast, 16 B unique), 1 bf16 `shared`, 1 bf16 store.
  Grid is always whole threadgroups (768 = 3×256, and 256 is a
  multiple of SIMD width 32), so no partial threadgroup and no
  bounds check is needed at any row count (round-3 boundary check,
  `hyp-1-combine-devolatilize.md` *Boundary checks* attempt-2).
- **Neighbours:** identical to A. Indexing is row-count
  independent straight-line code, so the six G2 passes carry the
  rounding argument to untested sizes by construction; only the
  six sizes are certified (boundary *can't see* list).
- **Cost:** see D. Body terms that are not unique traffic: one
  `idx/768` integer divide per thread and 768× redundant weight
  loads per row — bounded in `ineff-baseline-combine-2`.
- **Invariants:** the written fold is already the reference's
  association (round-2 territory checklist C: `col_reduce_small`
  folds `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`). Reassociating to any other tree,
  including the balanced `((p0+p1)+(p2+p3))`, changes f32 rounding
  on ppm of elements and fails G2 (round-1 CPU emulation, cited in
  round-2 `ineff-baseline-combine-1`); contracting any mul into its
  add does the same (section C). The arithmetic is therefore
  frozen; only data movement, mapping and launch shape may move.

### C. Header: `block-1.metal` — what the pragma leaves in the binary

- **What it is:** two lines, `#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF` and
  `#pragma clang fp contract(off)` (`block-1.metal:23-24`), wired
  by `"header_block": 1` — the only `spec.json` delta from the
  volatile starting point (`attempt-2/notes.md` *What changed*).
  `slots.build` passes the header text to `mx.fast.metal_kernel`
  (`slots.py:317-325`), which emits it before the generated kernel
  function, where FP-option pragmas take effect
  (`block-1.metal:6-13`; MLX help for `metal_kernel`: header is
  included before the main function).
- **Compile flags:** `slots.build` passes no `compile_options`, so
  MLX's default `math_mode` Safe applies
  (`.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/common/metal_kernel.h:7-15`).
  Without fast-math the compiler does not reassociate
  (`block-1.metal:19-22`); contraction is the only transform that
  could keep a product unrounded into its add, and
  `contract(off)` forbids exactly that fusion.
- **FMA or not — the evidence that exists:** no FMA *effect*
  survives. `grade.json` shows `differ 0 / max_ulp 0.0` at all six
  sizes (summed over 20 layers), while the contracted evaluation's
  fingerprint is known from the volatiles-free twin: 0 / 2 / 2
  differ decode, 6 / 50 / 130 prefill (round-3 territory checklist
  B; round-2 `ineff-baseline-combine-1`). Any surviving
  mul→add fusion in the four products or the three adds would
  reproduce that signature at ppm rate; it is absent at
  31.5M prefill elements, so the graded binary evaluates 4
  separate `fmul` + 3 separate `fadd` roundings (plus the bf16
  cast and bf16 add, neither of which has a mul to contract).
  The final line cannot contract in any case: `acc` is already a
  materialised local and `shared` is a load, not a product.
- **What remains unverified (not an inefficiency):** no `.air` /
  `.metallib` disassembly was produced. `xcrun metal` cannot run
  on this machine (`cannot execute tool 'metal' due to missing
  Metal Toolchain; use: xcodebuild -downloadComponent
  MetalToolchain` — checked 2026-11-04), MLX compiles in-process
  through the Metal framework so there is no kernel file on disk
  to inspect, and running MLX to force a compile is a GPU job an
  explorer must not start (tracking.md *Rules*). Which of the two
  spellings is load-bearing (the C99 `STDC` form is expected to be
  inert in Metal's C++-based language; the `clang fp` form is the
  operative one) is likewise unprobed: separating them needs two
  graded builder attempts, not explorer work. Functionally the
  pair as graded is proven; at instruction level the answer
  above is inferred from G2, labelled as such. Round 3's notes
  already named this probe (`attempt-2/notes.md` *Next change*:
  check the compiled binary for fma) — it is still open, and it
  changes no kernel decision until a toolchain or a re-grade
  exists, because G2 re-proves the effect on every grade.

### D. Cost table: `grade.json` and the chained floor

Measured, piece (`attempt-2/grade.json`, chained paired timing,
`check_candidate.py:191-251` — 20 layers linked by the `link`
kernel, candidate vs compiled in alternating repeats, `faster`
needs ≥22/30 wins). Floors at 200 GB/s peak and 5.2 TFLOPS peak
(`claude/GLOSSARY.md`); per-row traffic 9,232 B, ~7 f32 ops per
output:

| Size | Candidate | Compiled | Margin | Wins | BW floor | Compute floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decode 1 | 31.8 | 36.9 | 5.1 µs/layer (0.10 ms/step) | 24 | 0.05 µs | ~0.001 µs |
| decode 8 | 34.7 | 41.1 | 6.4 (0.13) | 27 | 0.37 | ~0.008 |
| decode 32 | 32.7 | 45.7 | 13.0 (0.26) | 30 | 1.48 | ~0.03 |
| prefill 127 | 38.2 | 64.0 | 25.8 | 30 | 5.86 | ~0.13 |
| prefill 1,016 | 100.9 | 281.8 | 180.9 | 30 | 46.9 | ~1.05 |
| prefill 2,048 | 198.0 | 556.2 | 358.2 | 29 | 94.5 | ~2.12 |

- **Decode is the chained floor.** Traffic + compute are
  ≤1.5 µs of a ~32–35 µs/layer measurement at every decode size;
  the rest is one dispatch + `link` + launch latency per layer,
  identical for candidate and compiled bar (both are timed
  through the same chain, `check_candidate.py:197-214,372-384`).
  Candidate time is flat in rows (31.8 → 32.7 for 32× the work),
  the signature of a fixed floor, already confirmed for this
  slot's shape in round 2 (`ineff-baseline-combine-2`, frozen).
  Absolute chained µs drift up to ~35% between runs on identical
  code (round-3 lesson, `attempt-2/notes.md` *Why the timing
  missed*), so only the same-run margins and win counts above
  are evidence; cross-run absolutes (e.g. attempt-1's 46.8 /
  42.0 / 49.2 in its hotter run) are machine state.
- **Prefill is body-shaped but not bandwidth-bound.** Candidate
  slope ≈0.094 µs/row/layer between 1,016 and 2,048 rows against
  the 0.046 µs/row bandwidth slope: ~95 GB/s achieved, about
  half of peak. Compiled slope ≈0.256 µs/row (~34 GB/s). The
  candidate's scalar, latency-shaped body (section B) therefore
  still beats the compiled reference's generic body by 2.8× at
  2,048 rows, while neither is close to peak bandwidth in the
  glossary's sense. Kind: overhead-bound throughout
  (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`), least so at large prefill.
- **Where the margin comes from.** The margin grows with rows
  (5.1 → 13.0 decode, 25.8 → 358.2 prefill) because it is a
  per-element body gap riding on a common fixed floor: at 1 row
  the floor compresses a ~2.8× body advantage into 5.1 µs and
  24 wins — the thinnest decode verdict in the slot (threshold
  22, `check_candidate.py:59-63,244-250`). That thinness, not
  any single size's median, is what G3's range rule then meets
  at 32×128 / 32×1024 (`claude/findings/muse-round-3.md` §1:
  combine fails alone vs `compiled-combine` there on overlap,
  no phase slower anywhere).

### E. Whether any bit-exact change widens the decode margin

No candidate survives the arithmetic. The kernel is already at
the minima on all three axes a bit-exact change may touch:

- **Arithmetic: frozen.** 4 muls + 3 adds + bf16 cast + bf16 add
  is the reference's own op count; every reassociation or
  contraction variant fails G2 (sections B–C). There is no
  seventh-op saving to take.
- **Bytes: minimal.** Every `y` element feeds exactly one output,
  `shared` and `out` are touched once, `weights` unique traffic
  is 16 B/row. Routing weights are strictly positive
  (sigmoid outputs normalised ×2.5, `slots.py:44-48`), so no
  zero-weight sparsity exists to skip reads for — and a
  data-dependent skip would still need the weight read first.
- **Launches: minimal.** One kernel per layer; zero is not a
  kernel. The remaining decode time is the shared dispatch
  floor (section D), which no body edit removes — round 1's
  staged/vectorised organisation and round 2's staged variant
  landed on the same floor (round-2 territory checklist E,
  frozen; re-bounded for this body in
  `ineff-baseline-combine-2`).

The three mapping changes a builder could still try, each
bit-exact by construction, bound as follows (predictions,
arithmetic in the inefficiency entry): removing the per-thread
`idx/768` divide with a 2-D grid (`grid ["768","rows"]`,
`thread_position_in_grid.y` as the row — expressible, since
`dim()` accepts literal and `rows` terms, `slots.py:283-293`);
staging the 4 weights per threadgroup instead of 768× broadcast
loads; and widening to one thread per 2–4 outputs (fewer threads,
weights loaded once per group of outputs). Each attacks
<1 µs/layer of body time under a ~32 µs floor — inside the
~5% same-kernel paired noise the brief warns of
(`claude/muse-agent-brief.md` *The piece timing*) and below
what 22/30 wins can certify. Threadgroup-size retuning
(128/512/768) changes only how the same 768·rows threads are
packed into the same single launch, so it cannot move the
dispatch term either. A `min_rows`/`max_rows` hand-off is
strictly narrowing here: `min_rows: 2` would hand the 1-row win
(5.1 µs, the set's 1-request combine contribution) to the
compiled reference, and `max_rows: 32` would hand away
25.8–358.2 µs/layer of prefill margin that G3's prompt time
currently banks. **Conclusion for builders: do not spend combine
attempts on widening decode margin; the slot's remaining G3
problem is 5-repeat spread at 32×1024, which only set
composition (the `g3` territory's question) or repeat count —
neither a kernel property — can move.** This matches round 3's
close (`hyp-1-combine-devolatilize.md` *Decision*: no further
kernel change worth making on 7 plain ops), now with the
round-4 hand-off surface checked as well.

## Relations

- **Fed by:** `baseline-experts` (`y`), `baseline-routing`
  (`weights`; the combine part is graded on reference weights, so
  routing exactness cannot save or fail this slot), shared expert
  (outside the slots, `shared`), `grader` (six-size G2, chained
  timing, `handed off` rules that never fire here), `g3` (the
  32×1024 set-margin question this slot's thin 1-row / 32-row
  verdicts feed).
- **Feeds:** residual add / next layer; the ready check's set
  (`muse-all`), where this kernel's 1-request speed is part of
  what lets a `min_rows` experts attempt pass at 1 request.

## Inefficiencies

- `ineff-baseline-combine-1` — the chained dispatch floor:
  ~32 µs/layer at decode against ≤1.5 µs of traffic + compute;
  already minimal at one launch, so no bit-exact change banks
  it (open; repriced for this kernel).
- `ineff-baseline-combine-2` — per-thread divide + redundant
  weight-broadcast loads: the only body terms left above the
  floor, bounded under 1 µs/layer (open; posted so the bound is
  verified, not chased).

## Files read

- `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/{spec.json,block-0.metal,block-1.metal,notes.md,grade.json}`
  — the code in the slot: launch surface, 7-op body, pragma
  header, builder account and the six-size verdict/margins.
- `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-1/{block-0.metal,block-1.metal,spec.json,grade.json,notes.md}`
  — the `noinline` twin: same body, call barriers, same verdict
  shape in a hotter run (cross-run drift control).
- `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1/block-0.metal`
  — the volatile predecessor (7 barriers the pragma replaces).
- `bench/grader/slots.py:44-52,97-119,283-343`,
  `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:59-63,152-163,191-251,253-271,352-400`
  — reference, MoE split, size expressions, G2, link chain,
  paired verdicts, hand-off handling.
- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232,251-258`
  — the combine line and its residual consumer.
- `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/mlx/include/mlx/backend/common/metal_kernel.h:7-15`
  — `math_mode` Safe default (no `compile_options` are passed).
- `claude/findings/muse-round-3.md` §§1–2,4,
  `claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md`,
  `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` (slots, piece timing, `min_rows`),
  `claude/GLOSSARY.md` (kind terms, peak figures).
- Frozen, cited not repeated:
  `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md`
  (volatile accounting, install path, op balance),
  `muse-spark/round-3/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-1.md`
  (twin swing +1.441 ms/step, confirmed),
  `muse-spark/round-3/implementation/hyp-1-combine-devolatilize.md`

  `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md`

{"path":"muse-spark/round-4/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-1.md","content":"# Inefficiency: baseline-combine-1 — chained dispatch floor, ~32 µs/layer at decode

- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-combine
- **Status:** open
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T21:44:10Z
- **Next:** verifier to check the floor arithmetic; no builder action predicted to bank it

## Slot

`combine`.

## What happens

The code in the slot
(`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/block-0.metal:26-42`,
`spec.json`: grid `rows*768`, threadgroup [256,1,1]) is already a
single fused kernel per layer — the 5-kernel reference chain
(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52` eagerly) collapsed to one launch,
20 per decode step. What remains at decode sizes is a flat
~32 µs per layer that does not move with rows (31.8 at 1 row,
34.7 at 8, 32.7 at 32; `grade.json`), while the work itself is
9,232 B/row of unique traffic and ~7 f32 ops per output. The
grader prices each layer through the same serial `link` chain
for every function timed (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:191-214`),
so the floor — one `mx.fast.metal_kernel` dispatch, command
encoding and launch latency at 3 / 24 / 96 threadgroups — is
shared with the compiled bar and cancels out of the margin; it
is the level the margin sits on, not the margin itself. The
same floor was confirmed for this slot's shape under the old
timing basis in round 2 (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-2.md`,
frozen); this entry reprices it for the pragma kernel under
round 4's chained paired grader. No `max_rows`/`min_rows` is
set, so no size hands off (`bench/grader/slots.py:338-339`).

## Cost

Per layer (peak 200 GB/s, 5.2 TFLOPS, `claude/GLOSSARY.md`;
measured, piece: `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/grade.json`):

- Kernels × fixed cost: 1 kernel/layer either way (candidate
  and compiled reference alike in the chain). Candidate
  measured 31.8 / 34.7 / 32.7 µs decode, 38.2 / 100.9 / 198.0
  prefill; compiled 36.9 / 41.1 / 45.7 and 64.0 / 281.8 / 556.2.
- Bytes ÷ peak: 9,232 B/row → 9,232 / 73,856 / 295,424 B decode
  = **0.05 / 0.37 / 1.48 µs**; 1,172,464 / 9,379,712 /
  18,907,136 B prefill = **5.86 / 46.9 / 94.5 µs**.
- Compute: 7 × 768 × rows FLOP = **~0.001 / 0.008 / 0.03 µs**
  decode, ~0.13 / 1.05 / 2.12 µs prefill.
- Remainder (measured − bytes − compute): **~31.7 / 34.3 /
  31.2 µs at decode (≥95% of the measured time)** and ~32 /
  53 / 101 µs at prefill (dispatch amortised over more rows;
  prefill slope ~0.094 µs/row ≈ 95 GB/s achieved, still half
  of peak). Over 20 layers the decode remainder is ~0.62–0.69
  ms of every decode step spent before any byte or FLOP of
  this slot is paid for — for the compiled bar too (its
  remainder is larger, which is the 5.1 / 6.4 / 13.0 µs/layer
  margin, 24 / 27 / 30 wins).

Absolute chained µs drift up to ~35% between runs on identical
code (round-3 `attempt-2/notes.md`), so the remainders above

## Slot

`combine`.

## What happens

Above the dispatch floor (`ineff-baseline-combine-1`), the
kernel body in the slot
(`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/block-0.metal:26-37`)
still does two things per thread that carry no unique
information:

1. `row = idx / 768u` (`:27`) — a 32-bit integer divide by a
   non-power-of-two, once per output element (768 divides per
   row per layer call), plus the `row*3072` / `row*768`
   multiplies that follow from it (`:31-32`).
2. `weights[wbase .. wbase+3]` (`:34-37`) — the same 4 float32
   weights of a row loaded independently by all 768 threads of
   that row: 768 × 4 loads × 4 B = 12,288 B of logical load
   traffic per row for 16 B of unique data. The bytes hit L1
   as a broadcast (unique DRAM traffic stays 16 B/row), so the
   cost is load-issue slots and latency, not DRAM bytes.

Everything else in the body is minimal: 4 strided-coalesced
bf16 loads, 7 f32 ops in the frozen fold, 1 bf16 load, 1 store
(territory entry, section B). Round 2 bounded this same
micro-path for the predecessor body and posted no entry
(`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-combine.md`
checklist E, frozen: expected saving <1 µs/layer, inside
run-to-run spread). This entry re-derives the bound for the
pragma kernel and posts it so the round-4 decode-margin
question has a verified ceiling instead of folklore.

## Cost

Per layer (peaks from `claude/GLOSSARY.md`; measured context:
`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/grade.json`,
candidate 31.8 / 34.7 / 32.7 µs decode, 38.2 / 100.9 / 198.0
prefill):

- Kernels × fixed cost: unchanged — these terms add no launch;
  they live inside the single kernel whose floor is
  `ineff-baseline-combine-1`.
- Bytes ÷ peak: unique traffic unchanged at 9,232 B/row
  (**0.05 / 0.37 / 1.48 µs** decode; **5.86 / 46.9 / 94.5 µs**
  prefill). The redundant weight loads add no DRAM bytes;
  priced (incorrectly, as an upper bound) at DRAM peak they
  would be 12,288 B/row = 0.06 / 0.49 / 1.97 µs decode and
  7.8 / 62.4 / 125.8 µs prefill — but they are served from L1
  at far above DRAM bandwidth, so the true byte cost is a
  small fraction of that bound; the divide is pure ALU
  (~5,376 / 43k / 172k divides' worth of issue at decode
  1 / 8 / 32 rows… per layer: rows×768 divides).
- Measured: no isolated measurement exists — the terms are
  inside the 31.8–198.0 µs/layer totals above and below the
  ~5% same-kernel paired noise the brief reports
  (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md` *The piece timing*: ~1.6 µs
  at decode levels). Two controls bound them from outside:
  round 1's staged/vectorised organisation (weights staged
  once, u64 loads, one barrier) measured the same floor as the
  unstaged kernel (17.9 / 16.1 / 18.1 vs 18.6 / 17.0 / 18.9
  µs/layer, independent basis, frozen citation in the
  territory entry), and round 3's two barrier mechanisms
  (call vs pragma, same indexing) both won every size on
  same-run verdicts without either showing an indexing effect.

## Kind

Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): neither bytes at peak
nor FLOPs at peak; issue/latency slivers under a dispatch
floor.

## Spans

`baseline-combine` only (index lines and load lines of the
single kernel). No other territory's code is touched by any
fix here.

## Predicted saving

Removing both terms bit-exactly is possible in principle —
row from `thread_position_in_grid.y` with a 2-D grid
(`slots.py:283-293` admits literal × `rows` products per grid
axis), weights staged once per threadgroup, or one thread per
2–4 outputs reusing one weight load set — and each variant
keeps the frozen 7-op fold untouched. Predicted saving if
removed (prediction, from the L1-bound above discounted by
the two controls): **≤0.5 µs per layer at decode 1 / 8 / 32
rows (≤0.01 ms per decode step) and ≤2 µs per layer at
prefill 127 / 1,016 / 2,048 rows**, i.e. at most a tenth of
the thinnest decode margin (5.1 µs/layer at 1 row) and below
paired-timing discrimination (needs ≥22/30 wins;
`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:59-63`). No phase trades
against the other: the same lines run at all sizes, and the
prefill ceiling is larger in µs but irrelevant to the
32×1024 set margin, which is decided in decode steps. The
entry's use is therefore negative: it caps what a
margin-widening combine attempt could win, so attempts are
not spent proving it kernel by kernel.

## Verdict

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
95|
96|## Tools and limits
97|
98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
99|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
100|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
101|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
102|
103|## Rules of this session

134|

144|

146|

150|    {
151|      "name": "fused_routing",
152|      "source_block": 0,
153|      "header_block": null,
154|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
155|      "outputs": [
156|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
157|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
158|      ],
159|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
160|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
161|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
162|      "init_value": null,

164|    }
165|  ],

170|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
171|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
172|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
173|- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows.

Use it when your kernels lose at the smallest decode sizes, such as 1 row ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)). G3 times whole requests: with 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so an attempt that hands off 1 row runs MLX's own code for the whole 1-request workload, and can pass G3 only in a set whose other kernels are faster there.
175|- **A hand-off is checked like the rest:** bit-exact at every G2 size. The piece timing reports a size it hands off as `handed off` instead of timing it (*The piece timing*, below).
176|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` and `min_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`.
