182|## How each attempt is judged
183|
184|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
185|
186|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
187|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
188|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
189|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
190|
191|   At every size:
192|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
193|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
194|
195|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
196|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
197|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
198|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
199|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
200|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
201|
202|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
203|
204|   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).
205|
206|   **From round 4, a set:** with more than one candidate, the ready check and G3 also time them all together (`muse-all`). When that passes, the candidates are ready together as a set, even where one fails alone, and G3 judges the set as one submission ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).
207|
208|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
209|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
210|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
211|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same`, `slower`, or `handed off` for a size your spec hands to the compiled reference); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
212|
213|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
214|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
215|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
216|- **Handed off** (from round 4): a size whose inputs your spec hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`, `min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is not timed against it. Its verdict is `handed off`, and your attempt's time there is the compiled reference's.
217|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size it doesn't hand off is, and at least one isn't handed off; `slower` when any size is; `handed off` when all are; and `not slower` otherwise.
218|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
219|
220|It is a guide; the ready check in the round, and Claude's G3 after it, decide.
221|
222|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

1|# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.
6|
7|## Hardware limits
8|
9|**Peak bandwidth**:
10|The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
11|_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed
12|
13|**Peak compute**:
14|The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
15|_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)
16|
17|**Achieved bandwidth**:
18|The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
19|_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)
20|
21|**Arithmetic intensity**:
22|Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
23|_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio
24|
25|**Ridge point**:
26|The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.
27|
28|**Roofline**:
29|The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.
30|
31|## Bottlenecks and fixes
32|
33|**Bandwidth-bound**:
34|A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.
35|
36|**Compute-bound**:
37|A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.
38|
39|**Overhead-bound**:
40|A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
41|_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)
42|
43|**Bottleneck**:
44|The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
45|_Avoid_: issue, slowness
46|
47|**Kernel**:
48|One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
49|_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)
50|
51|**Occupancy**:
52|The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
53|_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)
54|
55|**Knock-out**:
56|A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
57|_Avoid_: ablation
58|
59|**Baseline**:
60|The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.
61|
62|**Fix**:
63|One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
64|_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak

67|
68|**Prefill**:
69|Processing a request's whole prompt through the model before its first token is generated, in chunks of up to the engine's token budget per pass (2,048 tokens here).
70|_Avoid_: prompt phase (say prefill, or prompt processing)
71|
72|**Decode step**:
73|One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.
74|
75|**Decode rows**:
76|The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
77|_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency
78|
79|**Client concurrency**:
80|The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
81|_Avoid_: batch size

90|_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts

123|

Round 3 ran as Muse Spark (model `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, skill version 8) and submitted the reference in every slot: no candidate passed the ready check alone, and the skill then counted only candidates that pass alone. Round 4 changes three rules ([ADR 0015](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)): candidates that pass together in `muse-all` are `ready` as a **set**; an attempt may hand off inputs below `min_rows` as well as above `max_rows`; and a handed-off size is reported `handed off` instead of being timed. A slot's **baseline** is still its best attempt so far that passes the current G2, has `beats_compiled` true in the grader, and passes G3 ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). **No slot has a baseline.** The bar in every slot is the compiled reference, and a new attempt must beat it in the same grader run (no `--baseline` argument). 99|## 5. How round 3 worked
100|
101|The new rules held:
102|- every end-to-end number in *Ready to test* comes from the ready check, and predictions are labelled;
103|- `checker-final` found 7 rounding slips in the last digit and had them fixed before the round ended;
104|- when the fused experts kernel kept losing at 1 row, attempt-5 changed approach to an unfused path, and its ledger line says so.
105|
106|What went wrong:
107|- **Builders were spent on directions exploration had already ruled out:** experts attempt-2 and routing attempt-3.
108|- **Extra kernel launches cost more than they saved.** Routing attempt-3's added copy launch, about 2 to 3 µs per layer, flipped its decode from `faster` to `same`. Experts attempt-5's five launches instead of two cost about 18 µs per layer, part of its 2× loss at 1 row (`hyp-2-experts-prefill.md`, `hyp-3-routing-prefill.md`).
109|- **The thread limit cost two attempts.** Metal's limit per pipeline depends on the kernel's registers, 640 and then 576 threads here, while the grader checks only for 1,024. Routing attempts 2 and 4 failed G1 on it.
110|- **The grader timed identical code against itself.** Above `max_rows` an attempt runs the compiled reference, and the grader still timed it against the compiled reference. That judged routing attempt-1 `slower` at 2,048 rows on 8 wins of 30, and cost a re-grade of a byte-identical copy (attempt-6). From round 4 such a size is `handed off` (ADR 0015).
111|- **The set had no rule.** The skill said submitting together needs `muse-all` to pass, but made only single candidates `ready`. The lead read it strictly and submitted nothing. From round 4 a passing `muse-all` makes its candidates `ready` as a set (ADR 0015).
112|- **Absolute grader times drift up to twice between runs** on this machine, so comparing attempts across runs misleads; the round learned to compare ratios against the compiled reference from the same run.

# Territory: baseline-experts

- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-experts
- **Status:** done
- **Version:** 2
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T17:39:32Z
- **Next:** none — checklist filled, 2 inefficiencies posted, no notes to answer

## What it does

The `experts` slot of one MoE layer: for each row `r` and slot `j`,
`y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]`
with `e = inds[r, j]`. The code in the slot is now the round-2
starting point `muse-spark/round-2/kernels/experts/attempt-7`: one
fused per-pair kernel (512 threads per pair, `rows*4` threadgroups)
with interleaved gate/up and interleaved down behind a `rows >= 60`
branch — a `qvm` replica below 60 rows, a scalar `qmm_accum`
(`bfloat16`-rounded dequant, contiguous `BK=32` order) at/above.
It passes G2 bit-exact at all six sizes, beats compiled at 8/32
decode rows, and loses at 1 row and at every prefill size
(15–28× slower than compiled).

Round 2's `muse-spark/round-2/exploration/territory-baseline-experts.md`
(§A–§F, frozen) mapped the attempt-4 starting point, the reference,
and both MLX kernels; its three inefficiency entries are confirmed
and frozen. This entry cites them where they still hold and writes
only what is new: the attempt-7 code as slot code, the two-phase
timing that did not exist in round 2, and why the starting point
is no baseline.

## Checklist

### A. `block-0.metal` — fused per-pair kernel body (attempt-7)

Delta on round-2 §A (attempt-4 body).

- **Callers:** `spec.json` kernel `fused_experts_branch` (see §C),
  via `bench/grader/slots.py:303-345` (`build`) and
  `slots.make_moe_call` (`slots.py:97-119`), as in round-2 §A.
  Shapes new: prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows → 508/4,064/8,192 pairs
  (`slots.py:214-254`); decode 1/8/32 → 4/32/128 pairs. Grader
  times all six sizes chained (`check_candidate.py:345-368`).
- **Callees:** decode (`x_shape[0] < 60`): `qvm_gate_up_pair`
  (`block-0.metal:53-55`, one wave, simd 0–11, 4 idle) then
  `qvm_down_pair` (`:98-99`, 12 pairs in one wave, 4 idle).
  Prefill (`>= 60`): scalar `qmm_accum` — gate and up as two
  sequential `simd < 12` phases (`:61-71`), down in 2 waves
  (`:105-111`, wave 1 uses simdgroups 8–11 only). Silu-mul inline
  in both branches (`:77-85`), 384 of 512 threads active.
- **Data:** inputs/outputs unchanged from round-2 §A (11 inputs,
  `y` `[rows, 4, 768]` bfloat16 positional, `pair >> 2`, `e =
  inds[pair]`, `block-0.metal:16-21`). Threadgroup memory
  unchanged: `tg_x[768] + tg_gate/up/h[384]` = 3,840 B
  (`:24-27`). Thread registers new: two kernel-scope 32-float
  accumulators `p`, `q` (`:42-43`) shared across phases —
  attempt-6 proved three distinct arrays fail G1 at 512 threads
  (pipeline max 448; `attempt-7/notes.md:10-15`).
- **Neighbours:** unchanged from round-2 §A (routing `inds`
  before, combine after, any order/duplicates accepted).
- **Cost:** 1 kernel per layer call at every size. Grid
  `rows*2048` threads ÷ 512 = `rows*4` groups (4 at 1 row,
  8,192 at 2,048 rows). Weight bytes per pair unchanged at
  552,960 B (`attempt-7/notes.md:119-121`; round-2 §A
  arithmetic). Measured chained, this run
  (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-2/grade-phases-experts-attempt-7.json`,
  candidate vs compiled): 92.1 vs 78.6 (1 row), 162.8 vs 235.5
  (8), 515.3 vs 797.8 (32), 15,220.0 vs 960.8 (127), 119,154.4
  vs 4,306.0 (1,016), 240,681.1 vs 11,998.9 (2,048) µs/layer.
  Effective on pair bytes: 24.0 / 108.7 / 137.3 GB/s decode,
  18.5 / 18.9 / 18.8 GB/s prefill (200 GB/s peak,
  `claude/GLOSSARY.md:10`).
- **Invariants:** G2 passes with `differ == 0`, `max_ulp 0.0` at
  all six sizes (grade-phases file, `correctness`). The four
  bfloat16 rounding points kept (`:56-57,64,70,84,100-101,109`).
  Branch threshold `x_shape[0] >= 60` (`:22`) is the dispatch
  source value (round-2 §E/§F, frozen).

### B. `block-1.metal` — pair helpers and `qmm_accum`

Delta on round-2 §B (`qvm_block` replica).

- **Callers:** `block-0.metal` as in §A above. `qvm_block`
  (`block-1.metal:22-58`) is kept verbatim but now unused; its
  arithmetic is copied into the pair helpers
  (`block-1.metal:8-10`).
- **Callees:** `simd_sum` trees only (`:120-127,187-194`), one
  per accumulator (two per pair call). `qmm_accum` (`:206-230`)
  calls nothing: one thread per output, `BK=32` tiles in
  contiguous K order, `wq` rounded to bfloat16 before the
  multiply (`:225-226`).
- **Data:** per pair helper call two 32-output blocks; per
  `qmm_accum` call one output (`word = wb + (lane >> 3)`,
  `shift = (lane & 7) * 4`, `:217-218`), so 8 lanes share each
  weight word and all 32 share `S`/`B`/`xv[k]` per iteration.
- **Neighbours:** helpers read `tg_x` (gate/up) or `tg_h`
  (down) after barriers, as in round-2 §B. No barrier between
  the gate and up prefill phases (disjoint outputs,
  `block-0.metal:61-72`); barriers after `tg_x` (`:32`),
  after gate/up (`:73`), after silu (`:86`).
- **Cost:** decode per thread: gate/up 24 strided steps
  (`K=768`), down 12 merged steps (`K=384`), each step ~2×(2
  scale/bias + 4 weight words) + 64 dependent accumulates.
  Prefill per pair: 884,736 single-thread iterations
  (gate/up 384×768 each, down 768×384), each 1 W + 1 S + 1 B
  device load + 1 `tg` load on one serial accumulator —
  ~7.1 MB of scalar load issues per pair for 553 KB of
  unique weight bytes (8× W, 32× S/B redundancy; see
  ineff-baseline-experts-1). Serial depth per thread
  (simd < 8): 768 + 768 + 768 = 2,304 dependent iterations.
- **Invariants:** per-block decode order is `qvm_block`'s
  order (strided `k = lane, lane+32, …`, same term sequence,
  same `simd_sum`), so decode bits equal attempt-5's by
  construction; prefill order is contiguous per-output K,
  which G2 confirms equals `gather_qmm_rhs` bits (`differ
  0`) — the round-3 README *Refuted claims* records that
  scalar sums reproduce this MMA rounding.

Round 2's pairings run (plain MLX) found every pair within 0.5 ms of its parts' sum, but all three together with 8 requests 2.8 ms slower than their parts (+0.94 ms measured against −1.87 ms summed) — the second set of kernels to show it, so the cause is likely in how the step runs with all three slots replaced at that size, not in one kernel. Not explained. Every round-2 variant keeps the model's greedy tokens in both engines at 1 and 32 requests (round 1's change them with 32).
61:Confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the compiled reference (no slot has a baseline, so the reference is the bar everywhere). Savings span both phases now: decode shares use the plain-MLX step denominators 4.75 / 13.37 / 28.19 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 rows, prefill effects are prompt-time multiples and whole-request throughput from Claude's engine comparison. Exactness gates are solved in every slot — all three starting points pass G2 at all six sizes — so nothing below is blocked on correctness.
67:5. **Why all three slots replaced at once lose 2.8 ms with 8 requests.** Every pair adds up; all three together miss by 2.8 ms in plain MLX (round 2 pairs run), repeating round 1's shape. Until it is understood, per-slot piece wins may not compose into a G3 win. Claude's question 3. Carried as a constraint on every hypothesis; the ready check measures each candidate alone and all together, so round 3 sees composition inside the round.
93:| `g3` | "All three together" and item 5 of *What is left* — where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing (combine at 32, the three together at 8), and why. |
101:A decode step produces one token per request. On plain MLX with 128-token prompts the bare step takes 4.75 / 13.37 / 28.19 ms at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (Claude: `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md`, via round 1); in vLLM the unchanged step round 2 re-measured takes 5.442 / 14.524 / 30.470 ms (`claude/findings/muse-round-2.md` §3). A step is 867 kernels at 1 row, 987 at 32 rows, far below both hardware limits, so it is overhead-bound throughout. The MoE block (`MoE.__call__`, `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:217-232`) runs in all 20 layers of every step, in decode and in prefill chunks alike; the three slots mirror its split.
105:Round 3's starting points already fuse each slot to 1 kernel per layer (20/step per slot) and pass G2 bit-exact at all six sizes. What remains is not launch count or exactness but: prefill speed (experts' scalar branch, routing's staged path), in-step composition the grader cannot see (combine's volatiles, the three-way 8-request term), and the experts 1-row decode chain. No slot has a baseline, so every saving below is against the compiled reference.

{"path":"muse-spark/round-4/exploration/territory-g3.md","content":"# Territory: g3 — Claude's round-3 measurement, end to end vs piece by piece

- **Owner:** explorer-g3
- **Status:** exploring
- **Version:** 1
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T21:42:54Z
- **Next:** verifier to check ineff-g3-1..2; margin mechanism belongs to baseline-routing/baseline-combine, three-slot cause still open

## What it does

This territory is not code in the decode step. It is the measurement that decides whether round 3's attempts actually made the model faster: Claude's G3 of the routing+combine pair (routing attempt-6 + combine attempt-2) alone and together, the swarm's ready check of the same pair, the one-request long-prompt run, and the experts attempt-1 piece result that never reached G3, all written up in [claude/findings/muse-round-3.md](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md). Raw data in `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-3/`, `results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-3-long/` and `muse-spark/round-3/checks/ready-1/`. Frozen prior work: round 3's [territory-g3.md](../../round-3/exploration/territory-g3.md) and [ineff-g3-1.md](../../round-3/exploration/ineff-g3-1.md)–[ineff-g3-3.md](../../round-3/exploration/ineff-g3-3.md) (cited, not repeated). Its questions for round 4 are where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing now, what a set containing an experts attempt with `min_rows: 2` would predict at the four G3 workloads, and whether the rounds 1–2 three-slot interaction still stands in the way.

Every speed number below says its level and kind: **measured, piece** (grader `grade.json`, chained µs per layer), **measured, whole request** (ready check / G3, vLLM, 5 shuffled repeats, 256 generated tokens), or **prediction** (arithmetic shown, counting only the candidate's own measured effect). A combination is measured as one, never added up from its slots; sums of piece effects are labelled predictions.

## Checklist

### 1. Piece timing basis — the three starting points' `grade.json`

- **Callers:** `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` chained piece timing (20 layers' captured inputs, each call waiting for the previous; brief, *The piece timing*), re-run by Claude where noted. Files: `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/routing/attempt-6/grade.json`, `…/combine/attempt-2/grade.json`, `…/experts/attempt-1/grade.json`; Claude's re-grade of routing with the round-4 grader in `results/runs/2026-11-04-grader-hand-off/grade-routing-attempt-6.json`.
- **Callees:** G1 (compiles/runs), G2 (bit-exact at decode 1/8/32 rows and prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows), paired piece timing (30 alternating pairs per size; `faster` needs ≥22 wins).
- **Data:** chained µs per layer, candidate vs compiled reference. Routing attempt-6 (`max_rows: 32`): 51.7 vs 66.3 (1 row, 28 wins), 90.9 vs 104.0 (8, 27), 132.2 vs 152.0 (32, 25); prefill `same` (hand-off in effect: rows above 32 run compiled code). Combine attempt-2 (no hand-off): decode 31.8 vs 36.9 (24 wins), 34.7 vs 41.1 (27), 32.7 vs 45.7 (30); prefill 38.2 vs 64.0 (30), 100.9 vs 281.8 (30), 198.0 vs 556.2 (29) — `faster` at all six. Experts attempt-1 (`max_rows: 59`, no `min_rows`): 96.9 vs 86.6 (1 row, 5 wins, `slower`), 168.9 vs 238.2 (8, 29, `faster`), 554.7 vs 883.4 (32, 29, `faster`); prefill `same` at all three (hand-off runs compiled code). All three G2 `differ 0` at all six sizes.
- **Neighbours:** the original experts and shared expert run between routing and combine in the model; the grader tests the combine part with reference routing weights (brief, *The launch spec*). Absolute chained times drift up to ~35% between runs on this machine (round-3 lesson, carried in the round-4 README *Starting point*); only same-run paired verdicts and ratios transfer.
- **Cost:** piece-implied decode change vs the compiled reference (candidate − compiled) × 20 layers, ms per step: routing −0.292 / −0.262 / −0.396 at 1/8/32 rows; combine −0.102 / −0.128 / −0.260; pair (sum, prediction basis) −0.394 / −0.390 / −0.656; experts (as graded, without `min_rows`) +0.206 / −1.386 / −6.574. Vs the uncompiled reference (routing reference 71.9/113.0/150.8, combine 59.1/45.1/62.9 µs/layer): pair −0.950 / −0.650 / −0.976 ms/step. Kernel counts (whole step, piece 3 checks): pair removes 280 kernels/step at both 1 and 32 rows (967→687, 1087→807); vs `compiled-all` (867/987) it removes 180.
- **Invariants:** G2 bit-exact everywhere above, including the routing tie rule and the hand-off sizes; `beats_compiled` true for routing (`faster` decode, `not slower` prefill) and combine (`faster` both phases), false for experts on the 1-row decode size alone. This piece prices every gap below; it says nothing by itself about composition in the live step.

### 2. The swarm's ready check (`muse-spark/round-3/checks/ready-1/ready-verdict.json`)

- **Callers:** `bench/grader/check_ready.py` run by the round-3 lead at 2026-11-04T18:52:00Z over routing attempt-6 + combine attempt-2 (protocol block: vLLM, `1x128/8x128/32x128/32x1024`, 5 repeats, 256 tokens). Only this run's `pass` could make a candidate `ready` in round 3 (ADR 0013; round 4's set rule is ADR 0015).
- **Callees:** the same G3 harness as Claude's run (piece 3): token check at 1 and 32 requests, then decode-step period, prompt time and whole-request time per workload.
- **Data:** decode medians [min–max], ms/step (`medians` block). Base 5.470 [5.430–5.713] / 14.514 [14.482–14.541] / 30.186 [30.031–31.049] / 39.725 [39.611–39.912]; `compiled-all` 5.044 [5.016–5.269] / 14.075 [14.031–14.343] / 29.935 [29.822–29.975] / 39.530 [39.441–39.723]; `muse-all` (pair) 4.553 [4.545–4.611] / 13.629 [13.590–13.788] / 29.452 [29.295–29.496] / 38.942 [38.806–39.106]. Pair vs base: −0.917 / −0.885 / −0.734 / −0.783; vs `compiled-all`: −0.491 / −0.446 / −0.483 / −0.588 (−1.49% at 32×1024). Prompt medians, pair vs base: 46.1 vs 47.0 / 195.2 vs 201.4 / 759.5 vs 797.4 / 6415.5 vs 6589.5 ms; request medians 1232.1 vs 1463.1 / 3673.4 vs 3900.1 / 8273.7 vs 8481.4 / 16135.5 vs 16525.9 ms. Singles: `muse-routing` decode −0.38 / −0.31 / −0.59 / −0.48 vs base ([muse-round-3.md:39](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)); `muse-combine` −0.53 / −0.59 / −0.44 / −0.26, with one 1×128 repeat at 5.892 ms above the base minimum 5.430 (`medians.muse-combine.1x128.decode.max`).
- **Neighbours:** same kernels, same workloads and same bars as piece 3; the two runs differ only in machine state (swap 13.9–14.2 GB in Claude's run, [muse-round-3.md:19](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)) and repeat draws.
- **Cost:** verdicts (`variants` block): `muse-routing` fails vs `compiled-routing`, `muse-combine` fails vs base and vs `compiled-combine`, **`muse-all` passes vs both bars** (`pass: true`, decode `faster`, request `faster`) — the round-3 skill counted only alone-passing candidates, so nothing was submitted; under round 4's set rule this pair would have been `ready` as a set.
- **Invariants:** `same_tokens: true` for every variant at 1 and 32 requests; every failure in this run is a range overlap, no variant slower than either bar anywhere (`pass: false` at the top level is the alone-rule, not a slowdown).

### 3. Claude's G3, main run (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-3/`)

- **Callers:** `time_candidates.py vllm` run by Claude after the round ([muse-round-3.md:13–17](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)); verdicts in `g3-vllm.json`, repeats in `console-vllm.txt`, per-run records in `muse-vllm.jsonl`.
- **Callees:** token check (greedy tokens identical for every variant, both engines), then the three G3 times per workload: decode-step median period, prompt time, whole-request time. G3 passes a phase only when the 5-repeat ranges do not overlap the bar's (brief, *How each attempt is judged*).
- **Data:** decode medians [ranges], ms/step (`console-vllm.txt` summary block; cross-checked against `muse-vllm.jsonl` `period_median_ms` medians). Base 5.457 [5.403–5.468] / 14.337 [14.314–14.424] / 30.061 [29.755–30.308] / 39.410 [39.095–41.190]; `compiled-all` 4.991 [4.910–5.419] / 13.940 [13.916–14.017] / 29.779 [29.712–29.892] / 39.127 [38.912–39.400]; pair (`muse-all`) 4.555 [4.479–4.690] / 13.565 [13.491–13.619] / 29.231 [29.066–29.402] / 38.765 [38.589–39.080]. Pair vs base: −0.902 (−16.5%) / −0.772 (−5.4%) / −0.830 (−2.8%) / −0.645 (−1.6%); vs `compiled-all`: −0.436 / −0.375 / −0.548 / **−0.362 (−0.93% at 32×1024, ranges [38.589–39.080] vs [38.912–39.400] overlap)**. Prompts (prompt-time medians from `muse-vllm.jsonl`): pair vs base −3.1% / −1.6% / −2.7% / −2.8%, slower nowhere; whole requests vs base −14.1% / −5.6% / −2.1% / −2.4% ([muse-round-3.md:24–27,52–65](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)). Singles vs base (decode): routing −0.409 / −0.314 / −0.608 / −0.624; combine −0.555 / −0.511 / −0.453 / −0.484. Compiling the two reference slots alone (`compiled-all` vs base) gains −0.466 / −0.397 / −0.282 / −0.283 — about half the pair's gain at 1×128 is `mx.compile` of MLX's own code.
- **Neighbours:** identical inputs to piece 2; the verdict difference at 32×1024 (piece 2 passes, here `muse-all` vs `compiled-all` decode `same`) is repeat-draw luck at a ~1% margin, not a kernel difference ([muse-round-3.md:43–48](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)).
- **Cost:** `g3-vllm.json`: pair passes vs base (`pass: true`, decode `faster`, request `faster`) and fails vs `compiled-all` on the single 32×1024 decode overlap; singles fail alone (routing `same` as `compiled-routing` at 8×128; combine `same` as `compiled-combine` at 32×128 and 32×1024), again with no phase slower anywhere. Kernel counts exact and additive (`muse-vllm.jsonl` checks: base 967/1087 at 1/32 rows; pair 687/807; every variant `exact: true`).
- **Invariants:** same greedy tokens for every variant alone and together; the G3 range rule is unchanged for round 4 (ADR 0015, *Considered options*), so a ~1% median gap at 5 repeats is decided by chance in either direction — both runs' medians favour the pair everywhere.

### 4. Claude's G3, long prompts (`results/runs/2026-11-04-muse-round-3-long/`)

- **Callers:** same harness with `--settings 1x1024,1x7936 --max-model-len 8192` (one request; 7,936 tokens is the longest prompt fitting the 8,192-token context with 256 generated tokens).
- **Callees:** same three G3 times; decode rows stay 1 at both prompt lengths, so this piece isolates prompt length / context from decode rows.
- **Data:** decode medians, ms/step (`console-vllm.txt` summary): base 5.716 [5.613–5.859] at 1×1024, 8.207 [8.129–8.263] at 1×7936; `compiled-all` 5.296 / 7.767; pair 4.868 [4.752–4.911] / 7.280 [7.244–7.335]. Pair vs base −0.848 (−14.8%) / −0.927 (−11.3%); vs `compiled-all` −0.428 (−8.1%) / −0.487 (−6.3%) ([muse-round-3.md:73–82](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)). Prompt time −2.9% / −2.1%, whole request −13.8% / −6.4% vs base; throughput 152→176 and 56→60 tokens/s.
- **Neighbours:** same pair as pieces 2–3; only the workload changes. The absolute decode saving stays 0.85–0.93 ms/step however long the prompt is, while the step itself grows 5.7→8.2 ms with context — the saving is a fixed per-step slot cost, not a share of the step.
- **Cost:** `g3-vllm.json` (long): pair `g3: true` vs both bars at both prompt lengths; combine alone also `g3: true`; routing alone fails vs `compiled-routing` only. With one request the pair clears the compiled bar by 6–8%, far outside the repeat spread — the 32×1024 failure in piece 3 is not a prompt-length effect.
- **Invariants:** tokens identical (`exact: true`, kernel counts 967→687 at 1 row as in piece 3); a 7,936-token prompt is about half the whole request, so the whole-request gain (−6.4%) is smaller than the decode gain even though nothing is slower.

### 5. Experts attempt-1 and the ungraded `min_rows: 2` variant (prediction input)

- **Callers:** nobody yet — no experts attempt has been timed end to end since round 2's attempt-7 ([muse-round-3.md:97](../../../claude/findings/muse-round-3.md)). The round-4 direction is attempt-1's fused kernel with `min_rows: 2, max_rows: 59` added to `spec.json` (ADR 0015; brief, *The launch spec*): rows 1 run the compiled reference, rows 2–59 run the fused kernel, rows above 59 run the compiled reference.
- **Callees:** if graded, G1/G2 at all six sizes (1-row decode and all prefill sizes `handed off`, not timed vs the bar), then the ready check timing the set alone and all together.
- **Data:** measured, piece (piece 1): 96.9 vs 86.6 µs/layer at 1 row (`slower`), 168.9 vs 238.2 at 8, 554.7 vs 883.4 at 32 (`faster`); prefill `same`/hand-off. With `min_rows: 2` the 1-row piece time becomes the compiled reference's by construction (same code), so the experts decode effect vs the compiled reference is 0 / −69.3 / −328.7 µs/layer = **0 / −1.386 / −6.574 ms/step at 1/8/32 rows** (arithmetic: 69.3×20÷1000, 328.7×20÷1000; the round-4 README's ~1.4 / ~6.6 ms). Weight traffic unchanged: 552,960 B per (token, expert) pair, read once per pair by the fused kernel (round 3's `territory-baseline-experts.md` §A; owned by `baseline-experts`).
- **Neighbours:** in a set, routing runs before experts and combine after; the combine part in isolation receives reference routing weights, but the set as timed in `muse-all` runs the real chain. With 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so this slot runs MLX's own code for the whole 1-request workload and the set can pass G3 there only on the other slots' wins (brief, *The launch spec*, `min_rows`).
- **Cost:** no measured, whole-request cost exists. Everything in *What a set containing it would predict* below is a prediction from this piece plus pieces 2–3, and carries the piece-6 interaction as an untested subtraction.
- **Invariants:** attempt-1 is bit-exact at all six sizes as graded; a hand-off is checked the same way (bit-exact at every G2 size, brief). Rows 2–7 and 9–31 run the fused kernel under `min_rows: 2` but were never piece-timed (the grader times 1/8/32); steady-state G3 steps at 8/32 requests have 8/32 rows, so the prediction uses the 8/32-row deltas and assumes nothing about intermediate rows beyond G2 exactness.

### 6. Three slots at once, rounds 1–2 (frozen history)

- **Callers:** round 2's pairs run (plain MLX, each kernel alone, all pairs, all three) and the round 2 main/engine runs; frozen in round 3's [territory-g3.md](../../round-3/exploration/territory-g3.md) piece 5 and confirmed [ineff-g3-2.md](../../round-3/exploration/ineff-g3-2.md); round 1's instance in round 2's `ineff-g3-1.md` (frozen).
- **Callees:** decode-step timing only; no prefill piece basis for pairs/triples exists.
- **Data:** three-way interaction (all-three change − sum of the three alone changes) at 8 requests: **+2.804 ms/step (pairs, plain) / +2.858 (main, plain) / +2.128 (main, vLLM) / +2.435 (engine, vLLM)**; every pair within +0.36 ms of its parts' sum at 8; at 1 request +0.262 (inside the 0.275-wide base spread, not claimed); at 32 requests +0.192 (real, ~15× smaller than at 8). Round 1's 32-request three-way term (+2.8/+3.3 ms) did not recur with round 2's kernels (+0.19), so that one was a round-1-kernel property; the 8-request term recurred across two exact kernel sets.
- **Neighbours:** round 3 installed no experts candidate, so no run since has met this term; round 4's set (piece 5) meets it again with three different kernel versions (routing `max_rows: 32`, combine without volatile barriers, experts `max_rows: 59` + `min_rows: 2`).
- **Cost:** if the term recurs at its historical size, it subtracts 2.13–2.86 ms/step at 8 requests from any additive prediction and ~0.2 ms/step at 32 (see the prediction table's sensitivity row). Kernel counts stayed exactly additive in every run (−200−80−120 = −400 at 1 row) while time did not, so the cost is not launch count.
- **Invariants:** tokens exact in every combination; ranges never overlapped the base at 8 requests in any of the four runs — not repeat noise. Cause still open (serial-latency composition vs a three-kernel dispatch/occupancy interaction at 8 rows); no single-slot change is predicted to remove it.

## Where the end-to-end change differs from the piece timing, and why

Two gaps are live for round 4. A third and fourth round-3 gap are closed and recorded so nobody re-chases them.

1. **The pair at 32 rows, above all 32×1024: piece says −0.656 ms/step vs the compiled reference, G3 keeps −0.548 (32×128) and −0.362 (32×1024) in Claude's run.** Shortfall (G3 − piece, vs compiled): −0.042 ms/step at 1×128 (G3 beats the piece sum), +0.015 at 8×128, +0.108 at 32×128, **+0.294 at 32×1024** (+14.7 µs/layer; vs the uncompiled reference the 32×1024 shortfall is +0.331: piece −0.976 vs measured −0.645). In the swarm's run the same 32×1024 shortfall is only +0.068 (−0.588 measured vs −0.656 piece), so 0.23 ms/step of the Claude shortfall is run-to-run movement, the same order as the shortfall itself. What is solid in both runs: the median gap vs `compiled-all` at 32×1024 is 0.9% (Claude) / 1.5% (swarm) and the 5-repeat ranges overlap in Claude's run ([38.589–39.080] vs [38.912–39.400]) and miss in the swarm's — the verdict flips on the draw. Piece 4 rules out prompt length alone (at 1 row the piece sum transfers fully at 1,024 and 7,936 tokens: −0.428/−0.487 measured vs −0.394 piece), and piece 3 rules out token divergence and kernel count. The residual grows with decode rows (1→32) and again with context at fixed 32 rows (30.1→39.4 ms steps), while the slots' own cost is context-independent — consistent with a fixed in-step composition cost the chained timing cannot see, at a size (≤0.3 ms/step) that 5 repeats cannot separate from machine drift (swap 13.9–14.2 GB). Not explained beyond that; posted as [ineff-g3-1](ineff-g3-1.md) (open). The practical consequence is a margin requirement, not a correctness one: the set needs more than ~1% at 32×1024, or more repeats than G3 gives it.
2. **All three together at 8 requests: untested since round 2, and it decides the `min_rows` set.** The additive prediction for the set (next section) is −2.16 ms/step vs base at 8×128; the historical three-way term is +2.13 to +2.86 ms/step at exactly that workload (piece 6). If it recurs at even its smallest measured size, the set's 8×128 decode gain is gone (−2.158+2.128 = −0.030 ms/step); at its largest the set is slower than base (+0.70). At 32 requests the historical term (+0.19) barely dents the prediction (−7.40→−7.21 vs base). No new run constrains this: round 3 timed no experts variant end to end. Posted as [ineff-g3-2](ineff-g3-2.md) (open); the ready check, which times candidates alone and all together, is the first instrument that will see it in round 4.

5|# From round 4, candidates that pass together are ready as a set, and an attempt may hand off small inputs too
6|
7|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../../PROVENANCE.md).*
8|
9|**The change.** Round 3 showed three gaps in the rules ([Claude's measurement](../findings/muse-round-3.md)). On 2026-11-04 surucuonur chose to fix all three before round 4:
10|
11|1. **Ready as a set.** Round 3's routing and combine candidates each failed the ready check alone, on overlapping ranges, while the two together (`muse-all`) passed it. The skill made a candidate `ready` only when it passed alone, so the round submitted nothing. From round 4, when `muse-all` passes the ready check, all its candidates are `ready` together as a **set**. A set goes to G3 whole, and G3 judges it as `muse-all`.
12|2. **Hand off below a row count too: `min_rows`.** `max_rows` already sends inputs with more rows to `mx.compile` of the slot's reference ([ADR 0011](0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). The new `min_rows` in an attempt's `spec.json` does the same for inputs with fewer rows, so the kernels run only from `min_rows` to `max_rows`. Round 3's experts attempt-1 lost to the compiled reference only at 1 row: 96.9 against 86.6 µs per layer, while it took 168.9 against 238.2 at 8 rows and 554.7 against 883.4 at 32. Its only way to pass was to win at the size it is worst at.
13|3. **A handed-off size isn't timed.** The grader timed each handed-off size, which runs the compiled reference, against the compiled reference: the same code twice. In round 3 that noise judged routing attempt-1 `slower` at 2,048 rows, on 8 wins of 30, and cost a re-grade of a byte-identical copy. Now such a size is reported `handed off`. A phase is `faster` when every size the kernels run at is faster, and it needs at least one; `beats_compiled` is still one phase `faster` and none `slower`. G2 still checks every size, bit for bit.
14|
15|## How it works
16|
17|- **`bench/grader/slots.py`:**
18|  - `build()` reads `min_rows` as it reads `max_rows`: an integer of at least 1, at most `max_rows` when both are given.
19|  - The function it returns has `hands_off(rows)`, which says whether inputs with that many rows run the compiled reference.
20|- **`bench/grader/check_candidate.py`:**
21|  - At each size, a function that hands the rows off is not timed. It takes the compiled reference's times, so for `routing+combine` the part that hands off adds the same time to both sides.
22|  - A bar's verdict is `handed off` when neither side ran code of its own. Against a baseline that runs its own kernels there, the size is timed as before.
23|  - `judge()` leaves `handed off` sizes out of a phase. A phase whose sizes are all handed off is `handed off`.
24|- **`bench/grader/test_hand_off.py`:**
25|  - checks `build()` with a toy kernel at row counts on both sides of each bound, bit for bit, and that bad bounds are refused;
26|  - checks `judge()` on five sets of verdicts.
27|  - Passed on 2026-11-04.
28|- **A real attempt.** Claude re-graded round 3's routing attempt-6 (`max_rows` 32) with the changed grader ([results/runs/2026-11-04-grader-hand-off/](../../results/runs/2026-11-04-grader-hand-off/)):
29|  - G2 passes;
30|  - decode is `faster` at 1, 8 and 32 rows, on 29, 26 and 27 wins of 30;
31|  - the three prefill sizes are `handed off`;
32|  - `beats_compiled` is true.
33|- **The skill, version 9.**
34|  - The ready check makes a passing `muse-all` a set.
35|  - *Ready to test* names a set's attempts together.
36|  - Builders and boundary agents record `min_rows` and the sizes it hands off.
37|- **G3 and the ready check are unchanged.** They time whole requests, so a slot's kernels count wherever they run. With 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so an attempt that hands off 1 row runs MLX's own code for the whole 1-request workload. Alone it is then no faster than its compiled bar there, and it can pass G3 only in a set whose other kernels are faster with 1 request. The brief says so.
38|
39|## Consequences
40|
41|- **Round 3's pair qualifies for round 4.** Under the set rule, routing attempt-6 with combine attempt-2 would have been `ready` in round 3, because its `muse-all` passed the swarm's ready check. Claude's G3 failed the same pair against the compiled bar at 32 requests of 1,024 tokens, on overlapping ranges, so the pair is still no baseline.
42|- **A set is judged once.** Its parts are not judged alone, so a set can carry a part that only helps together with the others. G3 still requires the whole set to be faster than both bars, and to be slower nowhere.
43|- **The interaction of all three slots is untested.** In rounds 1 and 2, replacing all three slots at once lost about 2.8 ms with 8 requests, for an unknown reason ([round 2](../findings/muse-round-2.md), section 4). A set with an experts attempt meets that again.
44|
45|## Considered options
46|
47|- **A paired test on medians for the ready check and G3,** so that one outlier repeat can't sink a candidate, as it sank combine attempt-2 in round 3. Not chosen for round 4: it changes ADR 0011's rule for Claude's G3 too, and there was too little time to check it before the deadline.
48|- **Hand-off by an explicit list of row counts.** More flexible, but no attempt has needed more than one range, and two bounds are simple to check.

24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.

30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
58|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
59|
60|Reference:
61|
62|```python
63|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
64|```
65|
66|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
67|
68|### `routing+combine`
69|
70|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
71|
72|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
73|
74|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
75||---|---|---|---|
76|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
77|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
78|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
79|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
80|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
81|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
82|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
83|
84|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
85|
86|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
87|
88|```python
89|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
90|```
91|
92|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
93|
94|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.

98|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.

182|## How each attempt is judged
183|
184|The pass criteria were fixed before the first round. From round 2, G2 is exact and also covers the prefill, and the piece timing chains the layers ([ADR 0010](adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md)); round 1 was judged by the earlier rules, in which G2 allowed small rounding differences and tested decode steps only. From round 3, the piece timing and G3 time both phases, decode and prefill ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)); rounds 1 and 2 were timed on decode only.
185|
186|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs.
187|2. **G2, correct: identical to the reference, bit for bit.** The slot runs in every call of `MoE.__call__`, the prefill included, so it is tested on every layer's inputs at two kinds of size:
188|   - **a decode step:** inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows;
189|   - **a prefill:** the first chunk of a prefill with 128-token prompts, recorded while the grader runs it, at 1, 8 and 32 requests: 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. From 60 rows on, MLX's own experts kernel changes (`gather_qmm_rhs` instead of `gather_qvm`), and so does its rounding.
190|
191|   At every size:
192|   - **`routing`:** each row's 4 experts and their 4 weights equal the reference's, in the same order, since combine sums the pairs in that order. That includes the reference's choice between tied 4th and 5th experts.
193|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element equals the reference's.
194|
195|   **Why exact:** the end-to-end check below asks for the same greedy tokens, and greedy decoding turns any difference into different tokens. In round 1, routing weights within 10⁻⁵ of the reference, relative, changed 7 to 9 of 32 sequences.
196|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
197|3. **G3, faster, in vLLM.** Each workload runs 5 times in shuffled order: 1, 8 and 32 requests with 128-token prompts, and 32 requests with 1,024-token prompts, 256 generated tokens each. Three times are measured per run:
198|   - the **decode step**, the median period between steady steps;
199|   - the **prompt time**, until every prompt was processed;
200|   - the **whole request**, from sending the requests to the last token.
201|
202|   Against both the original model and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code, the attempt passes when the decode step or the prompt time is faster in every workload, neither is slower in any, and no whole request is slower. Faster and slower mean that the ranges over the repeats don't overlap.
203|
204|   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).
205|
206|   **From round 4, a set:** with more than one candidate, the ready check and G3 also time them all together (`muse-all`). When that passes, the candidates are ready together as a set, even where one fails alone, and G3 judges the set as one submission ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).
207|
208|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
209|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
210|- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
211|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same`, `slower`, or `handed off` for a size your spec hands to the compiled reference); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.
212|
213|**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
214|- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
215|- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
216|- **Handed off** (from round 4): a size whose inputs your spec hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`, `min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is not timed against it. Its verdict is `handed off`, and your attempt's time there is the compiled reference's.
217|- **Per phase:** decode (1, 8, 32 rows) and prefill (127, 1,016, 2,048 rows) are each `faster` when every size it doesn't hand off is, and at least one isn't handed off; `slower` when any size is; `handed off` when all are; and `not slower` otherwise.
218|- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.
219|
220|It is a guide; the ready check in the round, and Claude's G3 after it, decide.
221|
222|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and has `beats_compiled` true, or after 5 attempts. Name your final attempt per slot in `muse-spark/summary.md`; it goes to the end-to-end and G3 checks, which surucuonur's team runs after merging your branch.

44|def ref_routing(x, w_router, bias):
45|    scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)
46|    inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=K - 1, axis=-1)[:, :K]
47|    w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
48|    return inds, w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * SCALE

52|    return (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared

55|def ref_experts(x, inds, *weights):
56|    """The port's SwitchGLU on flat rows: [rows, D] and [rows, K] -> [rows, K, D]."""
57|    from mlx_lm.models.activations import swiglu
58|    from mlx_lm.models.switch_layers import _gather_sort, _scatter_unsort
59|
60|    gate, up, down = weights[0:3], weights[3:6], weights[6:9]
61|    xx = mx.expand_dims(x, (-2, -3))
62|    do_sort = inds.size >= 64
63|    idx, inv = inds, None
64|    if do_sort:
65|        xx, idx, inv = _gather_sort(xx, inds)
66|
67|    def qmm(a, w):
68|        return mx.gather_qmm(
69|            a,
70|            *w,
71|            rhs_indices=idx,
72|            transpose=False,
73|            group_size=32,
74|            bits=4,
75|            mode="affine",
76|            sorted_indices=do_sort,
77|        )
78|
79|    y = qmm(swiglu(qmm(xx, gate), qmm(xx, up)), down)
80|    if do_sort:
81|        y = _scatter_unsort(y, inv, inds.shape)
82|    return y.squeeze(-2)

304|def build(spec, sources, slot):
305|    """A function slot_inputs -> slot_outputs from Muse Spark's spec and Metal blocks.
306|
307|    With "max_rows" in the spec, inputs with more rows than that run the slot's
308|    reference under mx.compile instead of the kernels, so an attempt can keep
309|    prompt-sized inputs on MLX's own code (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md);
310|    with "min_rows", so do inputs with fewer rows than that
311|    (claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md). The function's hands_off(rows)
312|    says whether inputs of that many rows run the compiled reference.
313|    """
314|    slot_in, slot_out = SLOTS[slot]
315|    kernels = []
316|    for k in spec["kernels"]:
317|        header = "" if k.get("header_block") is None else sources[k["header_block"]]
318|        fn = mx.fast.metal_kernel(
319|            name=re.sub(r"\W", "_", str(k["name"])),
320|            input_names=list(k["inputs"]),
321|            output_names=[o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]],
322|            source=sources[k["source_block"]],
323|            header=header,
324|            atomic_outputs=bool(k.get("atomic_outputs", False)),
325|        )
326|        kernels.append((k, fn))
327|    missing = set(slot_out) - set(spec["slot_outputs"])
328|    if missing:
329|        raise ValueError(f"slot_outputs is missing {sorted(missing)}")
330|    min_rows, max_rows = spec.get("min_rows"), spec.get("max_rows")
331|    for key, v in (("min_rows", min_rows), ("max_rows", max_rows)):
332|        if v is not None and (isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, int) or v < 1):
333|            raise ValueError(f"bad {key} {v!r}")
334|    if min_rows is not None and max_rows is not None and min_rows > max_rows:
335|        raise ValueError(f"min_rows {min_rows} is above max_rows {max_rows}: the kernels would never run")
336|    compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])
337|
338|    def hands_off(rows):
339|        return (max_rows is not None and rows > max_rows) or (min_rows is not None and rows < min_rows)
340|
341|    def run(**inputs):
342|        rows = inputs[slot_in[0]].shape[0]
343|        if hands_off(rows):  # the compiled reference takes over
344|            out = compiled(*[inputs[n] for n in slot_in])
345|            return dict(zip(slot_out, out if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out]))
346|        env = dict(inputs)
347|        for k, fn in kernels:
348|            tg = [int(t) for t in k["threadgroup"]]
349|            if any(t < 1 for t in tg) or tg[0] * tg[1] * tg[2] > 1024:
350|                raise ValueError(f"bad threadgroup {tg}")
351|            outs = fn(
352|                inputs=[env[n] for n in k["inputs"]],
353|                template=[
354|                    (n, template_value(v)) for n, v in (k.get("template") or {}).items()
355|                ],
356|                grid=tuple(dim(g, rows) for g in k["grid"]),
357|                threadgroup=tuple(tg),
358|                output_shapes=[
359|                    tuple(dim(s, rows) for s in o["shape"]) for o in k["outputs"]
360|                ],
361|                output_dtypes=[DTYPES[o["dtype"]] for o in k["outputs"]],
362|                init_value=k.get("init_value"),
363|            )
364|            env.update(zip([o["name"] for o in k["outputs"]], outs))
365|        return {name: env[src] for name, src in spec["slot_outputs"].items()}
366|
367|    run.hands_off = hands_off
368|    return run

1|"""Grade one kernel attempt: compile it, test it on captured inputs, time it.
2|
3|The independent grader for the Muse agent's kernels (claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
4|G2 tests it on the inputs `slots.py capture` recorded from a real decode step
5|(1, 8 and 32 rows), and on every layer's inputs in a prefill, recorded as
6|it runs (127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows): every output must be identical to the
7|reference's, bit for bit, since only then are the model's tokens identical
8|(claude/adr/0010-exact-at-every-size.md). The timing runs at the same six
9|sizes and chains the 20 layers, so each call waits for the one before, as in
10|the model. The grader prints its verdict as JSON, and writes it to --out when
11|given. It writes into an attempt folder only when --out points there, as
12|the Muse agent's builders do with grade.json; load() reads only spec.json and
13|the block-N.metal files.
14|
15|  .venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt folder> <slot> [--out FILE]
16|      [--baseline [SLOT=]FOLDER ...]
17|
18|The candidate and the compiled reference are timed in alternating repeats, so
19|drift in the GPU's clocks reaches both alike. At each size the candidate is
20|"faster" when it wins at least WINS_NEEDED of the REPEATS paired repeats (a
21|one-sided sign test at p < 0.01), "slower" when it loses that many, and
22|"same" otherwise; the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5% between
23|medians, so comparing medians alone would pass on noise. `beats_compiled`
24|needs both phases, decode and prefill: faster at every size of one, slower
25|at none of the other (claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md).
26|
27|A size whose inputs the attempt hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`,
28|`min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is "handed off", not timed against
29|it: a phase is faster when every size the kernels run is, and needs one such
30|size (claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md). G2 still checks it.
31|
32|--baseline times an earlier, already graded attempt in the same run and adds
33|`beats_baseline`, judged the same way. From round 2 on, the bar is the
34|previous round's final attempt for the slot
35|(claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md). FOLDER alone is an attempt
36|for the same slot. For routing+combine, give either one routing+combine

97|def ulp_bf16(r):

103|def differences(g, r):

106|    differ = (g != r) & ~(np.isnan(g) & np.isnan(r))

197|def chained(fn, layers, names):
198|    """All 20 layers' calls, each one waiting for the one before, as in a decode step.
199|
200|    A call's smallest input is linked to the previous call's last output, the
201|    same for every function timed. Without the wait, the GPU overlaps the
202|    calls and hides a slow call's latency; mx.depends orders only the graph.
203|    """
204|    small = min(names, key=lambda n: layers[0][n].size)
205|    outs = []
206|    for layer in layers:
207|        args = {n: layer[n] for n in names}
208|        if outs:
209|            args[small] = link(args[small], outs[-1][-1])
210|        out = fn(**args)
211|        if isinstance(out, dict):
212|            out = list(out.values())
213|        outs.append(list(out) if isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) else [out])
214|    return outs

217|def timed(fn, layers, names):
218|    """Median µs per layer: the 20 layers' chained calls, then one wait for the GPU."""
219|    for _ in range(3):
220|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
221|    times = []
222|    for _ in range(REPEATS):
223|        t0 = time.perf_counter()
224|        mx.eval(chained(fn, layers, names))
225|        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers))
226|    return round(statistics.median(times) * 1e6, 1)

229|def paired_times(fns, layers, names):
230|    """Per-repeat µs per layer of each function, in rotating order within each repeat."""
231|    calls = [lambda f=f: mx.eval(chained(f, layers, names)) for f in fns]
232|    for _ in range(3):
233|        for call in calls:
234|            call()
235|    times = [[] for _ in fns]
236|    for i in range(REPEATS):
237|        for j in [(i + k) % len(fns) for k in range(len(fns))]:
238|            t0 = time.perf_counter()
239|            calls[j]()
240|            times[j].append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(layers) * 1e6)
241|    return times

253|def judge(verdicts):
254|    """Each phase's verdict from its sizes' verdicts, and whether the candidate
255|    beats the bar: faster at every size of one phase, slower at no size of the other.
256|
257|    Sizes "handed off" don't count. A phase is "faster" when every other size
258|    is, "slower" when any is, "handed off" when none is left, and "not slower"
259|    otherwise.

261|    phases = {}

264|        phases[phase] = (

267|            else "slower" if "slower" in sizes
268|            else "not slower"

271|    return phases, beats

364|                own = {name: False for name in times}
365|                for part, fn in fns.items():

1|# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.
6|
7|## Hardware limits
8|
9|**Peak bandwidth**:
10|The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
11|_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed
12|
13|**Peak compute**:
14|The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
15|_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)
16|
17|**Achieved bandwidth**:
18|The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
19|_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)
20|
21|**Arithmetic intensity**:
22|Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
23|_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio
24|
25|**Ridge point**:
26|The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.
27|
28|**Roofline**:
29|The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.
30|
31|## Bottlenecks and fixes
32|
33|**Bandwidth-bound**:
34|A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.
35|
36|**Compute-bound**:
37|A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.
38|
39|**Overhead-bound**:
40|A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
41|_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)
42|
43|**Bottleneck**:
44|The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
45|_Avoid_: issue, slowness
46|
47|**Kernel**:
48|One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
49|_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)
50|
51|**Occupancy**:
52|The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
53|_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)
54|
55|**Knock-out**:
56|A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
57|_Avoid_: ablation
58|
59|**Baseline**:
60|The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.
61|
62|**Fix**:
63|One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
64|_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak
65|
66|## Inference
67|
68|**Prefill**:
69|Processing a request's whole prompt through the model before its first token is generated, in chunks of up to the engine's token budget per pass (2,048 tokens here).
70|_Avoid_: prompt phase (say prefill, or prompt processing)
71|
72|**Decode step**:
73|One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.
74|
75|**Decode rows**:
76|The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
77|_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency
78|
79|**Client concurrency**:
80|The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
81|_Avoid_: batch size
82|
83|## Mixture of experts
84|
85|**Expert**:
86|One of the interchangeable feed-forward blocks in a layer; MobileMoE-S has 60 routed experts per layer.
87|
88|**Active experts**:
89|The experts the router picks for one token in one layer (4 for MobileMoE-S).
90|_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts
