# Territory: grader — round 4's three rule changes (ADR 0015)

- **Owner:** explorer-grader
- **Status:** done
- **Version:** 4
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T21:44:30Z
- **Next:** none — checklist complete (5 pieces), 0 inefficiencies posted (grader runs no decode-step kernels; see *Inefficiencies*); notes delivered under `## From other agents` in `territory-baseline-experts.md`, `territory-g3.md` and `territory-baseline-routing.md` (2026-11-04T21:44:11Z), checker note held in *Inefficiencies*; no notes on this entry to answer

## What it does

Round 3's entry ([`muse-spark/round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md`](../../round-3/exploration/territory-grader.md), frozen) mapped the grader through ADR 0011/0013: bit-exact G2 at six sizes, paired timing at all six sizes, two-phase `beats_compiled`, the `max_rows` hand-off, and the ready check that judged each `muse-*` variant on its own pass. Round 4 changes three rules ([ADR 0015](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)): an attempt may also hand off below `min_rows`; a handed-off size is reported `handed off` and is not timed against the compiled reference; and candidates that pass together as `muse-all` are `ready` as a **set**. This entry writes only that delta. G1/G2 mechanics, the spec language apart from the two bounds, `capture`, `gpu_lock`, the chained timing and the G3 range rule are cited to round 3, not re-described. The grader was not run and no GPU work was done for this entry; unit-test and re-grade results below are cited to ADR 0015, not re-measured.

## The exact boundary a round-4 solution must keep

A round-4 attempt is inside the boundary only if all five hold. This is the checklist the builders, the boundary agent and the checker grade against; each line names its source.

1. **Spec validity.** `min_rows` and `max_rows` in `spec.json` are each an integer of at least 1, booleans and floats refused, and `min_rows ≤ max_rows` when both are given — otherwise `build()` raises `ValueError` before any kernel runs and the attempt is a G1 failure ([slots.py:330-335](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); brief:174). For `routing+combine` each part's spec carries its own pair of bounds (brief:176).
2. **Inclusive kernel window.** The attempt's kernels run exactly when `min_rows ≤ rows ≤ max_rows` for the bounds it gives (a missing bound is open on that side), and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile` outside that window; `rows` is the first slot input's `shape[0]` ([slots.py:338-345](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Row-for-row: `hands_off(rows)` is `rows > max_rows or rows < min_rows` ([slots.py:338-339](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)), and `test_hand_off.py` pins the edges bit-for-bit: 8 and 59 run the kernel, 7 and 60 run the compiled reference, for `min_rows: 8, max_rows: 59` ([test_hand_off.py:69](../../../bench/grader/test_hand_off.py)).
3. **G2 bit-exactness at every size, handed off or not.** G2 runs the attempt's `run()` — hand-off dispatch included — on all 20 layers at 1, 8, 32, 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows and requires bit-for-bit equality with the plain reference, in order for routing (including the tied 4th/5th choice) and elementwise for combine/experts; timing runs only if G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:320-351](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:187-195,175). A handed-off size therefore tests `mx.compile(reference)` against the plain reference through the attempt's own dispatch, which is why the boundary also includes compiled==reference at the six sizes (round-3 entry §2; [ADR 0011:34](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). For experts the window must also sit on the right side of MLX's 60-row kernel switch (`gather_qmm_rhs` from 60 rows, different rounding): a decode-built experts kernel may run only below 60 rows, i.e. `max_rows ≤ 59` ([slots.py:219-220](../../../bench/grader/slots.py); round-3 entry §2). Inside the window the reference still changes behaviour once: `ref_experts` sorts the pairs from 16 rows (`inds.size >= 64`, [slots.py:62](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)), so a kernel running at both 8 and 32 rows must match the unsorted and the sorted reference, both on the `gather_qvm` side of 60.
4. **Piece-timing phase rule.** At each timed size the verdict is `faster` with ≥22 wins of 30 paired repeats, `slower` with ≥22 losses, else `same` ([check_candidate.py:244-250](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). `judge()` drops `handed off` sizes from their phase: a phase is `faster` only when **every** size the kernels run at is `faster` and at least one such size exists, `slower` when any timed size is `slower`, `handed off` when none is left, else `not slower`; `beats_compiled` is true iff one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower` ([check_candidate.py:253-271](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:217-218). One `same` at a timed size blocks the bar; one `slower` anywhere fails it.
5. **Whole-request rule, and the set.** The ready check and G3 time whole requests in vLLM at 1×128, 8×128, 32×128, 32×1024 (5 repeats, 256 tokens), require the same greedy tokens at 1 and 32 requests, and pass a variant only when decode or prompt is `faster` (non-overlapping ranges) in every workload and nothing — decode, prompt or whole request — is `slower` anywhere ([check_ready.py:47-56,131-161](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py); [time_candidates.py:163-201](../../../bench/grader/time_candidates.py)). From round 4, when `muse-all` passes, its candidates are `ready` together as a set even where one fails alone, and G3 judges the set as one (skill step 4; brief:206; [ADR 0015:11,42](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)). The converse also binds: with 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so an attempt with `min_rows: 2` runs MLX's own code for the whole 1×128 workload and can pass G3/the ready check only inside a set whose other kernels are faster there (brief:174; [ADR 0015:37](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).

## Checklist

### 1. `slots.py` `build()` — `min_rows`/`max_rows` and `hands_off` (slots.py:304-368)

- **Callers:** `check_candidate.load` ([check_candidate.py:70-77](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)), and through it `time_candidates.Variants`/`implementations` and the ready check — so the same dispatch, bounds included, runs in G2, the piece timing, G3 and the ready check. For `routing+combine`, `load` splits the folder spec into per-part specs and builds each part separately, so each part hands off by its own bounds ([check_candidate.py:76-77](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py); brief:176).
- **Callees:** `mx.fast.metal_kernel` per spec kernel (built once per `build` call), and `compiled = mx.compile(REFERENCE[slot])`, also built once per call whether or not the spec gives bounds ([slots.py:336](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). `run()` calls `compiled(*inputs)` in slot-input order and re-zips to slot outputs on a hand-off ([slots.py:341-345](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)).
- **Data:** unchanged from round 3 (`SLOTS`, brief slot tables); the only new data is the two optional spec integers. `rows` is read from the first slot input's `shape[0]` for both dispatch and grid evaluation ([slots.py:342](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)).
- **Neighbours:** before it, the spec validation refuses a bad bound as a `ValueError`, which `check_candidate` reports as G1 (`result["error"]`, [check_candidate.py:401-402](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); after it, `run.hands_off` is the attribute the timing loop consults (piece 2). The threadgroup product ≤1024 check is unchanged ([slots.py:348-350](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)); threadgroup memory is still not checked (round-3 *can't see* item 8 stands).
- **Cost:** `build` launches no kernel itself. The hand-off branch is one Python comparison per `run()` call; in G3/ready-check serving that call happens per layer per step through `make_moe_call`, and any wrapper cost there is inside the whole-request times, not the piece timing (piece 2, *can't see* item 2). No new measured number is claimed here.
- **Invariants:** the inclusive window and the refusal rules in *The exact boundary* items 1–2; validation rejects `bool` explicitly because `True` is an `int` in Python ([slots.py:331-333](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)), and `min_rows > max_rows` is refused with "the kernels would never run" ([slots.py:334-335](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). What `build` does **not** check: that the window sits on the right side of 60 for experts, or anything about rows between the tested sizes (see *What each tool still cannot see*).

### 2. `check_candidate.py` — handed-off sizes not timed, `judge()` and `beats_compiled` (check_candidate.py:244-271, 352-400)

- **Callers:** builders, `.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py <attempt> <slot> [--out FILE]`; no `--baseline` this round — no slot has one (round-4 README *Starting point*), so the only bar is `compiled`. The `--baseline` path still exists and its handed-off rule differs (below), which a reader of a baseline grade must not confuse with the compiled bar.
- **What is new — exclusion, not a tie.** Per part and size, the timing loop builds `together = {candidate, compiled[, baseline]}` and then drops every function except `compiled` whose `hands_off(rows)` is true, so a handing-off function is never run in `paired_times` at that size ([check_candidate.py:372-380](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Its per-repeat times are then taken from the compiled function's repeats (`paired.get(name, paired["compiled"])`) and summed across parts as before ([check_candidate.py:381-384](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). Consequences in the printed verdict: at a fully handed-off size (vs the compiled bar) there is a `vs_compiled: "handed off"` and **no** `wins_vs_compiled` key, and the candidate's reported median equals the compiled median by construction ([check_candidate.py:386-394](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). The unpaired `reference` median is still timed at every size ([check_candidate.py:371](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)) — informational only, as in round 3. This removes round 3's defect exactly: identical code can no longer be judged `slower` on paired noise (routing attempt-1's 2,048-row verdict, re-graded `same` by attempt-6; round-4 README *Refuted claims*).
- **What is new — the `own` rule and the baseline exception.** `own[name]` records whether a function ran code of its own in **any** part at that size ([check_candidate.py:364,382](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). A size's verdict against a bar is `handed off` only when neither the candidate nor that bar ran its own kernels there: `if not (own["candidate"] or own[bar])` ([check_candidate.py:387-390](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). For the compiled bar `own["compiled"]` is never set, so the rule reduces to "candidate handed off in every part". Against a `--baseline` attempt that runs its own kernels at a size the candidate hands off, the size **is** timed as before — candidate repeats copied from compiled against the baseline's own repeats ([ADR 0015:22](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)). For `routing+combine` the summing is per part before wins are counted (round 3 §1 stands), so one part handing off while the other runs still times the size, on the summed repeats.
- **What is new — `judge()`.** It filters `handed off` verdicts out of each phase before judging ([check_candidate.py:262-269](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); the phase rule and `beats_compiled` are *The exact boundary* item 4. The five synthetic cases in `test_hand_off.py` pin them (piece 4). G2 is untouched: correctness still runs at all six sizes through the dispatch, and timing still runs only when G2 passes ([check_candidate.py:349-352](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).
- **Cost:** the timing still chains 20 layers × 30 paired repeats per timed size (round 3 §1); handed-off sizes now cost one compiled timing instead of two identical ones per part. The one real-attempt evidence that the new reporting works end to end is Claude's re-grade of round 3's routing attempt-6 (`max_rows: 32`) with this grader: G2 passes, decode `faster` at 1/8/32 on 29/26/27 wins of 30, the three prefill sizes `handed off`, `beats_compiled` true ([ADR 0015:28-32](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).
- **Invariants:** `WINS_NEEDED` is still 22 of 30 (one-sided sign test, p < 0.01, [check_candidate.py:56-63](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); size labels still carry the phase prefix (`rows ` / `prefill rows `) that `judge()` splits on ([check_candidate.py:57,358](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)). A phase with every size handed off can never supply the required `faster` phase: an attempt that hands off everything beats nothing (`judge` case "everything handed off", piece 4).

- **The set rule, precisely.** The audit fills `judged[v]` for **every** `muse-*` variant — each single slot and `muse-all` — with `pass = g3[v]["g3"] and same_tokens` ([check_ready.py:152-161](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)). The parts are still timed alone in the same run (the variants are all required by the audit), so the set reading costs no extra GPU run; a set's parts are not required to pass alone, but `muse-all` must still pass both bars and keep the tokens (`same_tokens` for `muse-all` at 1 and 32 requests, [check_ready.py:131-140,154-157](../../../bench/grader/check_ready.py)).

- **Invariants:** G3 and the ready-check protocol are unchanged ([ADR 0015:37](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)): a slot's kernels count wherever they run in a whole request, so the hand-off that the piece timing forgives is fully visible here — in particular at 1×128, where a `min_rows: 2` slot contributes the compiled reference's code, not its kernels (boundary item 5). Claude's post-round G3 stays the authority (round-3 entry §5).

## Worked example: an experts attempt with `min_rows: 2, max_rows: 59`

The round-4 README's ungraded direction (round-4 README *What is left* item 1): round 3's experts attempt-1 kernels plus this window. `hands_off(rows)` is true at 1 row (`1 < 2`) and at every row above 59 ([slots.py:338-339](../../../bench/grader/slots.py)). Graded with no `--baseline`, so the only bar is `compiled`:

| Size | Phase | Who runs | G2 | Piece verdict vs compiled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 row | decode | compiled reference | compiled vs plain reference, bit-exact required | `handed off` — not timed; no `wins_vs_compiled`; candidate median = compiled median |
| 8 rows | decode | attempt's kernels | kernels vs `gather_qvm` reference, unsorted pairs | timed: `faster` iff ≥22/30 wins, `slower` iff ≥22 losses, else `same` |
| 32 rows | decode | attempt's kernels | kernels vs `gather_qvm` reference, sorted pairs (from 16 rows) | timed, same rule |
| 127 rows | prefill | compiled reference | compiled vs plain reference (`gather_qmm_rhs` side) | `handed off` |
| 1,016 rows | prefill | compiled reference | same | `handed off` |
| 2,048 rows | prefill | compiled reference | same | `handed off` |

Phase arithmetic ([check_candidate.py:253-271](../../../bench/grader/check_candidate.py)): decode keeps only 8 and 32 rows, so decode is `faster` iff **both** are `faster`, `slower` iff either is `slower`, else `not slower`. Prefill has no timed size left, so it is `handed off`. `beats_compiled` is therefore true exactly when 8 and 32 rows are both `faster`; a `same` at either makes decode `not slower` and `beats_compiled` false, and a `slower` at either makes it false with decode `slower`. For scale only (prediction, not a grade): round 3's attempt-1 kernels timed 168.9 vs 238.2 µs per layer at 8 rows and 554.7 vs 883.4 at 32 in their own run, while losing 96.9 vs 86.6 at 1 row ([ADR 0015:12](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md); round-4 README *Per slot: experts*) — under the old rule that single `slower` made `beats_compiled` false; under this window the 1-row size is removed from the phase instead of having to be won. - **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes, longer for an attempt much slower than the reference at the prefill sizes; stop one that runs past 15.
- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.

- **`max_rows`** (optional, an integer of at least 1): inputs with more rows than this skip your kernels and run the slot's reference under `mx.compile`. Use it to keep prefill-sized inputs on MLX's own code when your kernels are built for decode sizes; MLX switches its own experts kernel at 60 rows.
- **`min_rows`** (optional, from round 4; an integer of at least 1, at most `max_rows` when both are given): inputs with fewer rows than this run the compiled reference too, so your kernels run only from `min_rows` to `max_rows`. Use it when your kernels lose at the smallest decode sizes, such as 1 row ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)). G3 times whole requests: with 1 request every decode step has 1 row, so an attempt that hands off 1 row runs MLX's own code for the whole 1-request workload, and can pass G3 only in a set whose other kernels are faster there.
- **A hand-off is checked like the rest:** bit-exact at every G2 size. The piece timing reports a size it hands off as `handed off` instead of timing it (*The piece timing*, below).
- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot, `max_rows` and `min_rows` included: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
   **From round 3, the same G3 runs inside the round too:** the lead's **ready check**, `bench/grader/check_ready.py`, with every candidate in one call. It also requires the same greedy tokens, and audits its own log. Only its passing verdict makes an attempt `ready`; Claude's G3 after the round decides. The skill says when the lead runs it ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)).

   **From round 4, a set:** with more than one candidate, the ready check and G3 also time them all together (`muse-all`). When that passes, the candidates are ready together as a set, even where one fails alone, and G3 judges the set as one submission ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)).

**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
- or the correctness results per size: for routing, the rows that differ; for combine and experts, the elements that differ and the largest gap in units in the last place; with the first example;
- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer` per size: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, its wins against the compiled reference and the verdict (`faster`, `same`, `slower`, or `handed off` for a size your spec hands to the compiled reference); then `phases_vs_compiled` and `beats_compiled`.

**The piece timing** runs the slot at the six G2 sizes: the 20 layers' captured decode inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows, and the 20 layers' first prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows. Each layer's call waits for the previous one's output, as in the model: one small kernel links them, the same for every function timed. Without that wait, the GPU overlaps the 20 calls and hides how long one takes; in round 1, an experts kernel 29% faster on overlapped calls was 66% slower on chained ones at 1 row.
- **Paired repeats.** Your attempt and the compiled reference run in alternating order, 30 times.
- **Per size:** your attempt is `faster` when it wins at least 22 of the 30 pairs, `slower` when it loses at least 22, and `same` otherwise. Medians alone would pass on noise: the same kernel timed twice differs by up to 5%.
- **Handed off** (from round 4): a size whose inputs your spec hands to the compiled reference (`max_rows`, `min_rows`) runs the bar's own code, so it is not timed against it. Its verdict is `handed off`, and your attempt's time there is the compiled reference's.

- **`beats_compiled`** is true when one phase is `faster` and neither is `slower`.

def judge(verdicts):
    """Each phase's verdict from its sizes' verdicts, and whether the candidate
    beats the bar: faster at every size of one phase, slower at no size of the other.

    Sizes "handed off" don't count. A phase is "faster" when every other size
    is, "slower" when any is, "handed off" when none is left, and "not slower"
    otherwise.
    """
    phases = {}
    for phase, prefix in PHASES.items():
        sizes = [v for size, v in verdicts.items() if size.startswith(prefix) and v != "handed off"]
        phases[phase] = (
            "handed off" if not sizes
            else "faster" if all(v == "faster" for v in sizes)
            else "slower" if "slower" in sizes
            else "not slower"
        )
    beats = "faster" in phases.values() and "slower" not in phases.values()
    return phases, beats

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write faster MobileMoE-S kernels, for decoding and prompt processing
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|A request goes through two phases: **prompt processing** (the prefill), which runs its whole prompt through the model, and **decoding**, one step per generated token. An improvement must hold in both: faster in one, and no slower in the other ([ADR 0011](adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A kernel that speeds up the decode step but slows the prefill is not an improvement.
12|
13|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
14|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
15|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
16|
17|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
18|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
19|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
20|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
21|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
22|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
23|
24|## The slots
25|
26|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the call: 1 to 32 in a decode step, up to 2,048 in a prefill chunk. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
27|
28|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
29|
30|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
31|
32|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
33||---|---|---|---|
34|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
35|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
36|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
37|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
38|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
39|
40|Reference:
41|
42|```python
43|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
44|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
45|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
46|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
47|```
48|
49|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
50|
51|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
52|
53|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
54||---|---|---|---|
55|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
56|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
57|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |

# Attempt 2 — builder-1-b, direction (b): FP-contract-off pragma barrier

First attempt in this direction (round 3, `hyp-1-combine-devolatilize`,
slot `combine`, baseline `none`). Builds on the starting point
`muse-spark/round-2/kernels/combine/attempt-1`, which passes G1+G2 and
`beats_compiled` but fails G3 (+1.051 ms/step in vLLM at 32 requests).

## What changed

Only the barrier mechanism. Grid (`rows*768`), threadgroup [256,1,1],
index/base lines, inputs/outputs and the final
`bfloat(acc) + shared[sbase]` line are verbatim from the starting
point. The seven `volatile float` locals (`p0..p3`, `s01`, `s012`,
`acc`) become seven plain `float` locals with the identical 7-op
sequence, and a new header block (`block-1.metal`, wired via
`"header_block": 1` — the only `spec.json` delta) disables FP
contraction for the kernel:

```metal
#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF
#pragma clang fp contract(off)
```

MLX emits `header` before the main function, so the pragmas precede the
kernel definition, which is where FP-option pragmas take effect. No
`volatile` anywhere in code, no `__attribute__((noinline))` helpers,
no extra functions, calls, or memory traffic of any kind.

Why this is contraction-proof: with contract(off) the backend may not
fuse any fmul+fadd into an fma — this is the compiler's own
contraction switch, so there is no transform left that can keep a
product unrounded into its consumer add. Each of the 7 statements is
then one rounded f32 op on register values: the same 7 materialisation
points, same fold order `((p0+p1)+p2)+p3`, same two bfloat16 roundings
as the starting point. Reassociation needs no pragma: it is off without
fast-math flags, and the grader sets none. The proof is G2 itself: any
surviving contraction shows the starting point's old signature (decode
0/2/2, prefill 6/50/130 differ).

## Inefficiency removed

`ineff-baseline-combine-1` (confirmed): the seven volatiles' 7 stores +
7 loads per output (56 B/thread of thread-private traffic, 43,008
B/row/layer) stall the decode step (+7.1/+25.4/+72.1 µs/layer vLLM)
and the 32×128 prompt (+1,501.7 ms twin). The pragmas keep every value
in registers — ~10 live floats, no spill pressure — so the barrier
costs zero bytes and zero instructions. Same fix covers both phases:
both run these identical lines.

## Prediction (µs per layer, chained paired basis)

Starting point (re-grade `grade-phases-combine-attempt-1.json`, via
`ineff-g3-1`): decode reference/candidate 52.8/45.7 @1, 71.2/47.9 @8,
87.0/64.6 @32; compiled 53.4/56.4/69.1. Prefill candidate
62.8/226.5/273.0 vs compiled 66.1/271.6/520.4.

Arithmetic:

- Slot traffic unchanged: 9,232 B/row ÷ 200 GB/s = 0.05 / 0.37 / 1.48
  µs decode, 5.9 / 46.9 / 94.5 µs prefill. Floor dominates decode.
- Spill floor removed: 43,008 B/row ÷ 200 GB/s = 0.22 / 1.7 / 6.9 µs
  decode, 27 / 218 / 440 µs prefill — an upper bound the quiet grader
  chain mostly does not price (the inefficiency entry), so decode is
  predicted at the starting point ±5% paired noise, prefill
  same-or-slightly-better.
- Predicted candidate: **45 / 47 / 63** decode, **61 / 220 / 265**
  prefill. Margins to compiled (≈8/9/6 decode, ≈5/50/255 prefill)
  reproduce the starting point's 28–30/30 wins: `faster` at all six
  sizes, both phases `faster`, `beats_compiled` true.
- G1 pass, G2 differ 0 / max ULP 0.0 at all six sizes.

The piece prize is keeping `beats_compiled`; the real prize (vLLM
≈0.5 ms/step at 8 requests, ≈1.4 ms/step at 32; order-1-s prompt
recovery) is invisible to the piece timing by construction and needs
the ready check.

## max_rows

None. The kernel runs identical lines at all sizes, combine has no
MLX kernel switch underneath, and the boundary's grader note says no
hand-off is needed for this hypothesis's direction.

## What this attempt leaves unmeasured

For the hypothesis entry's **Unverified** list: the in-step stall
recovery (only the ready check / G3 at 32 requests shows it);
exactness at row counts other than the six graded ones (boundary tool
`check_sizes.py` can probe 25 sizes incl. 59/60/61); the 33–126 band;
sizes above 2,048; prefill beyond the first seeded-random chunk;
whether the pragma pair is honoured by any toolchain other than the
graded one (irrelevant to the verdict, which runs on this one).

## Verdict

G1 pass, G2 pass at all six sizes, `beats_compiled` true. Baseline is
`none`, so there is no `beats_baseline` bar. Single grade run,
2026-11-04T18:05:21Z, verdict in `grade.json`.

- Correctness (differ / max ULP, summed over 20 layers): decode 1/8/32
  rows 0 / 0.0 each; prefill 127/1,016/2,048 rows 0 / 0.0 each.
  First difference: none. The pragma pair disables contraction: the
  plain-`float` stepwise fold is bit-exact everywhere the volatiles
  were, with no `volatile`, no helper calls, no memory traffic.
- Timing (µs per layer, reference / compiled / candidate, wins,
  verdict): rows 1: 59.1/36.9/**31.8** (24, faster); rows 8:
  45.1/41.1/**34.7** (27, faster); rows 32: 62.9/45.7/**32.7** (30,
  faster); prefill 127: 85.1/64.0/**38.2** (30, faster); prefill 1,016:
  419.6/281.8/**100.9** (30, faster); prefill 2,048: 828.9/556.2/
  **198.0** (29, faster). Same-run margins to compiled: −5.1/−6.4/−13.0
  decode, −25.8/−180.9/−358.2 prefill. `phases_vs_compiled`: decode
  faster, prefill faster; `beats_compiled` true.

### Why the timing missed the prediction (>20%)

Predicted decode 45/47/63 and prefill 61/220/265 from the re-grade's
absolute medians; measured 31.8/34.7/32.7 and 38.2/100.9/198.0 —
−25 to −55%. The miss is the anchor, not the kernel: chained absolute
µs drift run to run with machine state. In this same run the
*unchanged* compiled reference timed 36.9/41.1/45.7 decode vs
53.4/56.4/69.1 in the re-grade and 55.5/56.8/72.8 in builder-1-a's
run minutes earlier — a ~35% swing on identical code — while the
eager reference swung the other way at rows 1 (59.1 here vs 52.8
re-grade). Absolute chained medians therefore do not transfer across
runs; the valid evidence is the same-run paired verdict, which is
`faster` at all six sizes (24–30/30 wins) with both phases `faster`.
Corroborating cross-check on the same-run basis: builder-1-a's
noinline attempt (different run, hotter machine) shows the same shape
— `faster` everywhere with large prefill margins (−23.2/−173.7/−402.0
vs mine −25.8/−180.9/−358.2) — so both devolatilizations agree the
piece timing sees part of the spill prize at prefill sizes. Lesson:
predict combine piece times as same-run margins to compiled, never as
cross-run absolutes. (Noted in `ineff-baseline-combine-1.md`.)

Next change if hardening is wanted: none for this slot on the piece
basis — exact everywhere and `beats_compiled` with margin. The open
question is the vLLM step/prompt recovery, which only the ready check
can show; if it under-delivers, the next probe is whether the pragma
leaves any backend transform the volatiles also blocked (e.g. check
the compiled binary for fma), not another barrier shape.

# Inefficiency: baseline-combine-1 — chained dispatch floor, ~32 µs/layer at decode

- **Owner:** explorer-baseline-combine
- **Status:** confirmed
- **Version:** 2
- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T21:47:11Z
- **Next:** verifier to check the floor arithmetic; no builder action predicted to bank it

## Slot

`combine`.

## What happens

The code in the slot
(`muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/block-0.metal:26-42`,
`spec.json`: grid `rows*768`, threadgroup [256,1,1]) is already a
single fused kernel per layer — the 5-kernel reference chain
(`bench/grader/slots.py:51-52` eagerly) collapsed to one launch,
20 per decode step. What remains at decode sizes is a flat
~32 µs per layer that does not move with rows (31.8 at 1 row,
34.7 at 8, 32.7 at 32; `grade.json`), while the work itself is
9,232 B/row of unique traffic and ~7 f32 ops per output. The
grader prices each layer through the same serial `link` chain
for every function timed (`bench/grader/check_candidate.py:191-214`),
so the floor — one `mx.fast.metal_kernel` dispatch, command
encoding and launch latency at 3 / 24 / 96 threadgroups — is
shared with the compiled bar and cancels out of the margin; it
is the level the margin sits on, not the margin itself. The
same floor was confirmed for this slot's shape under the old
timing basis in round 2 (`muse-spark/round-2/exploration/ineff-baseline-combine-2.md`,
frozen); this entry reprices it for the pragma kernel under
round 4's chained paired grader. No `max_rows`/`min_rows` is
set, so no size hands off (`bench/grader/slots.py:338-339`).

## Cost

Per layer (peak 200 GB/s, 5.2 TFLOPS, `claude/GLOSSARY.md`;
measured, piece: `muse-spark/round-3/kernels/combine/attempt-2/grade.json`):

- Kernels × fixed cost: 1 kernel/layer either way (candidate
  and compiled reference alike in the chain). Candidate
  measured 31.8 / 34.7 / 32.7 µs decode, 38.2 / 100.9 / 198.0
  prefill; compiled 36.9 / 41.1 / 45.7 and 64.0 / 281.8 / 556.2.
- Bytes ÷ peak: 9,232 B/row → 9,232 / 73,856 / 295,424 B decode
  = **0.05 / 0.37 / 1.48 µs**; 1,172,464 / 9,379,712 /
  18,907,136 B prefill = **5.86 / 46.9 / 94.5 µs**.
- Compute: 7 × 768 × rows FLOP = **~0.001 / 0.008 / 0.03 µs**
  decode, ~0.13 / 1.05 / 2.12 µs prefill.
- Remainder (measured − bytes − compute): **~31.7 / 34.3 /
  31.2 µs at decode (≥95% of the measured time)** and ~32 /
  53 / 101 µs at prefill (dispatch amortised over more rows;
  prefill slope ~0.094 µs/row ≈ 95 GB/s achieved, still half
  of peak). Over 20 layers the decode remainder is ~0.62–0.69
  ms of every decode step spent before any byte or FLOP of
  this slot is paid for — for the compiled bar too (its
  remainder is larger, which is the 5.1 / 6.4 / 13.0 µs/layer
  margin, 24 / 27 / 30 wins).

Absolute chained µs drift up to ~35% between runs on identical
code (round-3 `attempt-2/notes.md`), so the remainders above
are same-run levels, not transferable absolutes; the flatness
in rows and the win counts are the stable part.

## Kind

Overhead-bound (`claude/GLOSSARY.md`): far below both peak
bandwidth and peak compute at decode; at prefill still only
~half of peak bandwidth, so overhead/latency-shaped there too.

## Spans

`baseline-combine` (the single launch and its spec), `grader`
(the link chain that prices the floor identically for every
function). Explicitly not the kernel body's arithmetic, which
section B of the territory entry shows is at its op minimum.

1|// Header for the devolatilized combine kernel (direction b: compiler
2|// contraction switch, no volatile, no helper calls).
3|//
4|// The Metal compiler FP-contracts mul+add pairs into FMAs by default,
5|// which keeps products unrounded into their consumer add and breaks the
6|// reference's per-op f32 rounding. The two pragmas below switch
7|// contraction off for the kernel function defined after this header
8|// (MLX emits `header` before the main function; `help(mx.fast.
9|// metal_kernel)`). With contraction off, the backend may not fuse any
10|// fmul+fadd into an fma, so each mul and each add in the body rounds
11|// once to f32 with its value living in a register — the same 7
12|// materialisation points as the starting point's seven volatiles, with
13|// zero thread-private memory traffic and no extra instructions.
14|//
15|// Both spellings are given: the standard C99 form and the Clang form.
16|// Either one alone disables contraction for the function; the second is
17|// belt and braces against pragma-dialect drift. They must live here, not
18|// in the body: FP-option pragmas take effect for functions defined after
19|// them, and the body is inside the generated function. Reassociation
20|// needs no pragma: the compiler does not reassociate without fast-math
21|// flags, and the grader passes none (slots.build sets no
22|// compile_options, so math_mode stays "safe").

---
name: muse-round
description: Run one round of the Muse agent on the MobileMoE-S kernels as a swarm. Explorers map the code and measurements into a shared analysis; then competing builders write and grade fused Metal kernels for the top inefficiencies. From round 2 on, the round starts from the previous rounds' results and must beat their best attempts. Both phases are tracked in shared documents.
---

# One round of the Muse agent: a swarm explores, then builds

*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed on main and tagged `muse-code-era` before the first Muse Code session; each later version is committed before the round that uses it. [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*

**Skill version 10.** This file, the role cards and tracking.md are versioned together; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists every version. Each round records the version it ran (see *Versions* in tracking.md).

You are the **lead** of a Muse Code session in your own worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. The first prompt names the Meta model you run as, the name your commit subjects start with, and the co-author line every commit ends with. `claude/muse-agent-brief.md` fixes the task, the slots, the tools and limits, the grader command and the pass criteria (G1, G2). Four ADRs change it in five ways:

1. **Harness** ([ADR 0006](../../../claude/adr/0006-muse-spark-in-muse-code.md)). You are a Muse Code session, not a Claude Code one. Muse Code adds no trailer, so you write the first prompt's co-author line on every commit yourself (see *Commits*).
2. **No attempt limit and no stop rule** (ADR 0006). The brief's *When a slot stops* no longer applies: you decide when a slot is done. Every graded attempt is committed, so the history shows every try.
3. **A swarm** ([ADR 0007](../../../claude/adr/0007-muse-spark-swarm.md)). Helpers explore and build; you coordinate and commit.
4. **Files** (ADR 0007, [ADR 0009](../../../claude/adr/0009-rounds-build-on-each-other.md)). Each round writes in its own **round folder**: round 1 at the top of `muse-spark/`, round N from 2 on in `muse-spark/round-<N>/`. It holds `exploration/` and `implementation/`, the round's shared documents, which replace `strategy.md`; `kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<M>/`; and `summary.md`. tracking.md writes it `<round>/`.
5. **Rounds build on each other** (ADR 0009). A finished round's files are frozen: read them and cite them, and the hooks refuse any change to them. From round 2 on, a slot may have a **baseline**: the best attempt so far that passes the current G2 and that Claude's G3 accepted: against the unchanged model and the compiled reference, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither ([ADR 0011](../../../claude/adr/0011-decode-and-prefill.md)). A new attempt must beat it in the same grader run. A slot without one has a **starting point** instead: an earlier attempt to build from, which Claude's measurement names, with what kept it from being a baseline.

The rest of the brief stands. The goal: kernels that make whole requests faster. In the grader they pass G1 and G2 and have `beats_compiled` true, faster in one phase, decode or prefill, and slower in neither (ADR 0011), and where the slot has a baseline `beats_baseline` true too, because they remove a cause you can name. Then the **ready check**, the same G3 Claude runs after the round, run by you inside it, must pass them before they are `ready` ([ADR 0013](../../../claude/adr/0013-measure-what-you-claim.md)). A faster decode step bought with a slower prefill is no improvement, and a claim no one measured is no result. An attempt may hand the inputs outside a row range it names to the compiled reference: those above `max_rows`, such as prefill-sized ones, and from round 4 those below `min_rows`, such as the 1-row decode step (the brief's launch spec, [ADR 0015](../../../claude/adr/0015-sets-and-hand-off-below.md)). The Muse agent was Muse Spark in round 1, Muse Wonder in round 2 ([ADR 0008](../../../claude/adr/0008-muse-wonder.md)) and Muse Spark's contributor model in round 3 ([ADR 0012](../../../claude/adr/0012-muse-spark-contributor-unattended.md)), and is Muse Wonder again in round 4, the last round ([ADR 0014](../../../claude/adr/0014-muse-wonder-last-round.md)); the first prompt names the model you run as, and documents from earlier rounds say the model of their round. No one approves your tool calls during the round, so the rules here are yours to keep.

## The swarm

| Role | Name | Task | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lead** (you) | | Start the helpers, keep the two READMEs, settle clashes, commit | this file |
| **Explorer** | `explorer-<territory>` | Map one territory into entries, and find where it loses time | [explorer.md](explorer.md) |
| **Verifier** | `verifier` | Check every inefficiency against its sources | [verifier.md](verifier.md) |
| **Builder** | `builder-<n>-<letter>` | Write and grade one solution for one hypothesis: one attempt | [builder.md](builder.md) |
| **Boundary agent** | `boundary-<n>` | Write what a hypothesis's solution must keep identical, and check passing attempts against it | [boundary.md](boundary.md) |
| **Checker** | `checker-<n>`, `checker-final` | Check every speed claim against the file it cites: a hypothesis's before it closes, and the round's final claims | [checker.md](checker.md) |

You don't explore, build or grade yourself; the one GPU job you run is the ready check (step 4). Start each helper with a prompt of this shape:

> You are `<name>`, a `<role>` in round `<N>`'s swarm; this round writes in `<round folder>`. Read `.agents/skills/muse-round/<card>` and `.agents/skills/muse-round/tracking.md`, then: `<task>`.

[tracking.md](tracking.md) describes the shared documents (the two phase folders, their READMEs, entries and logs) and the rules every agent keeps. Read it before starting anyone. Up to 12 agents run at once, you included.

**A checkpoint** is what you do each time a helper returns, and whenever the log shows something to settle:
1. **Read the log.** Read the phase log since your last checkpoint.
2. **Settle clashes.** When two entries describe one cause, keep the fuller one and set the other's status to `superseded by <entry>`. When two helpers work on one item, redirect one of them (`subagent_send_message`). Log what you decided.
3. **Refresh the tracker.** Update the phase README's tracker table, and raise the version of each hypothesis entry that changed.
4. **Raise the version.** Raise the phase README to its next version, and add its line to `## Versions`, naming the entries that changed and their versions (see *Versions* in tracking.md).
5. **Commit** the phase folder, plus any attempt that came back, as that version (see *Commits*).

## The round

### 0. Find where you are

- Run `git log --oneline main -1`, then `git tag --list -n1 'muse-round-*'`, which lists the finished rounds. **This round** is one more than the highest; with none, it is round 1. Its folder is `muse-spark/round-<N>/` (round 1: `muse-spark/`).
- `git log --oneline --grep '^Muse ' muse-code-era..HEAD` lists the Muse agent's commits of every round.
- **From round 2 on,** read Claude's measurement of the previous round, `claude/findings/muse-round-<N-1>.md`. It has the G3 results and names each slot's baseline or starting point. If it is missing, stop and reply "Claude's measurement of round <N-1> is missing": this round builds on it.
- If this round's folder already exists, a session stopped partway: carry on from its READMEs' last versions.
- Read the brief.

**Done** when you can name the round number and its folder, and from round 2 on each slot's baseline or starting point and the latest G3 results.

### 1. The starting point (from round 2 on)

This is the round's plan, built on what the earlier rounds learned. Read:
- the previous rounds' final exploration and implementation READMEs and `summary.md`;
- the `notes.md` of each baseline or starting-point attempt;
- Claude's measurement.

Then write the opening of this round's `exploration/README.md` (set up as in step 2.1), a section **Starting point**:
- **Per slot:**
  - the baseline, or the starting point where there is none, and its piece timing;
  - its G3 effect, and how that compares with what was predicted, with the reason where Claude's measurement gives one;
  - what keeps a starting point from passing G2, and where the attempt still spends its time.
- **What is left:**
  - the confirmed inefficiencies not yet built or not fully removed, ranked by predicted saving against the baselines, or the reference where a slot has none;
  - the slots not yet tried, for example `routing+combine`;
  - the recommendations outside the slots.
- **Refuted claims,** which no one chases again.

1|# The swarm's shared documents, and the rules every agent keeps
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Part of the [muse-round skill](SKILL.md). [Who made what](../../../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|Every agent of the round reads this file. The documents below are how the swarm shares what it knows and how surucuonur follows the round while it runs, so keep them current as you work, not at the end.
6|
7|## The round folder and its two phase folders
8|
9|`<round>/` is this round's folder: `muse-spark/round-<N>/` from round 2 on (round 1's is `muse-spark/` itself). The lead's prompt names it.
10|
11|| Folder | Phase | Holds |
12||---|---|---|
13|| `<round>/exploration/` | Exploration | the analysis: `README.md`, territory and inefficiency entries, `log.md` |
14|| `<round>/implementation/` | Implementation | the report: `README.md`, hypothesis entries, `log.md` |
15|
16|Kernels go in `<round>/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/`, numbered from 1 in each round; the grader reads any attempt folder it is given.
17|
18|**Earlier rounds' folders are frozen.** Read them and cite them by path; write what you add in this round's entries. The hooks refuse a change to any file a finished round left.
19|
20|Each folder has three kinds of document:
21|
22|- **`README.md`.** The phase's document. Only the lead writes it, refreshing it and raising its version at every checkpoint. It opens with its version line and the tracker table below.
23|- **Entries.** One file per territory, inefficiency or hypothesis. The owner keeps it current, and other agents append notes.
24|- **`log.md`.** One line per event, from every agent, appended only.
25|
26|## Versions
27|
28|Every shared document carries a version number, so a reader knows which version they're looking at, and git holds every version.
29|
30|**Phase versions.** Each README opens with its version line:
31|
32|```markdown
33|**Version:** v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · skill version 10
34|```
35|
36|- **Who raises it:** the lead, at every checkpoint, and each version is exactly one commit.
37|- **The commit:** its subject names the version, `<name>: exploration v5: <what changed>`, where `<name>` is the Muse agent's name from the lead's first prompt. `git log --grep 'exploration v5:'` finds it, and `git diff` between two such commits shows what changed.
38|- **The changelog:** the README ends with `## Versions`, one line per version, newest first, naming the entries that changed and their new versions:
39|
40|```markdown
41|- v5 · 2026-11-04T09:40Z · split quantized-kernels in two · changed: territory-quantized-kernels v4, ineff-quantized-kernels-2 v2
42|```
43|
44|**Entry versions.** Each entry's status block has a `Version` line, starting at 1:
45|- **Territory and inefficiency entries:** the owner raises it with every change to its own text. The verifier raises it when it writes the verdict.
46|- **Hypothesis entries:** the lead raises it at each checkpoint where the entry changed, builders' and the boundary agent's sections included.
47|- **Notes:** a note under `## From other agents` leaves the version alone. The owner raises it when folding the note in.
48|
49|**Times.** Every time you write, in a version line, a status block, a tracker row, a note or a log line, is the output of `date -u +%FT%TZ` run at that moment. Never estimate or round one.
50|
51|## The README trackers
52|
53|Exploration, `exploration/README.md`:
54|
55|| Territory | Agent | Status | Inefficiencies | Updated |
56||---|---|---|---|---|
57|| `quantized-kernels` | `explorer-quantized-kernels` | exploring | `ineff-quantized-kernels-1` (confirmed), `-2` (open) | 2026-11-04 09:40Z |
58|
59|Implementation, `implementation/README.md`:
60|
61|| Hypothesis | Slot | Builders | Attempts: G1, G2, µs per layer at 1 / 8 / 32 rows (compiled) | Status |
62||---|---|---|---|---|
63|| `hyp-1-fused-gather` | `experts` | `builder-1-a`, `builder-1-b` | 3: pass, pass, 41 / 55 / 180 (48 / 70 / 260) | hardening |
64|
65|From round 2 on, where the slot has a baseline, the attempts column also gives its time from the same run, and whether `beats_baseline` is true.
66|
67|## Entries
68|
69|Each entry opens with a status block that its owner keeps current:
70|
71|```markdown
72|- **Owner:** explorer-quantized-kernels
73|- **Status:** exploring
74|- **Version:** 3
75|- **Updated:** 2026-11-04T09:40Z
76|- **Next:** read the 32-row dispatch of affine_gather_qmm
77|```
78|
79|Entries are named so that two agents never pick the same name:
80|- `<round>/exploration/territory-<territory>.md`
81|- `<round>/exploration/ineff-<territory>-<n>.md`, numbered by the explorer of that territory
82|- `<round>/implementation/hyp-<n>-<slug>.md`, numbered by the lead
83|
84|**Another agent's entry:** append under its `## From other agents` heading, starting with your name and the time. The owner's text stays as written, so two agents never overwrite each other. The owner reads these notes and folds in what holds.

86|### Territory entry
87|
88|1. Status block (statuses: `exploring`, `done`).
89|2. **What it does** in the decode step, in a few lines.
90|3. **The checklist** below, filled in for each piece of code or table in the territory.
91|4. **Relations:** which territories feed it and which it feeds, with the data passed.
92|5. **Inefficiencies:** links to the entries this territory raised.
93|6. **Files read**, and what each one gave.
94|
95|### Inefficiency entry
96|
97|1. Status block. The statuses are `open`, `confirmed`, `refuted` and `superseded by <entry>`; only the verifier sets `confirmed` or `refuted`.
98|2. **Slot:** `routing`, `combine`, `experts`, or `outside the slots`.
99|3. **What happens:** what the code does, and where (file and lines).
100|4. **Cost** at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step and at the prefill's 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows: kernels × the fixed cost per kernel, bytes ÷ peak bandwidth, and the measured time with the table it comes from.
101|5. **Kind:** overhead-bound, bandwidth-bound or compute-bound, in the terms of `claude/GLOSSARY.md`.
102|6. **Spans:** the territories involved.
103|7. **Predicted saving** if removed, in µs per decode step at 1, 8 and 32 rows and per prefill chunk at 127, 1,016 and 2,048 rows, with the arithmetic. A saving in one phase that costs the other is not one.
104|8. **Verdict**, written by the verifier: each claim checked, and the result.
105|
106|### Hypothesis entry
107|
108|1. Status block. The lead owns it; the statuses are `boundary`, `building`, `hardening`, `candidate` (passes the grader's gates and its boundary check, signed by its checker), `ready` (a ready check passed it) and `dropped`.
109|2. **Inefficiency** it removes, the slot, and from round 2 on the slot's baseline folder, or `none` and its starting point.
110|3. **Boundary**, written by the boundary agent: what the solution must keep identical (see `boundary.md`).
111|4. **One section per builder:** its direction, its attempts (folder, predicted and measured µs per layer at the six sizes with each size's verdict, G1, G2, `beats_compiled`, and where the slot has a baseline its time and `beats_baseline`), and what each attempt taught.
112|5. **Boundary checks** of the attempts that passed G2.
113|6. **Decision:** the best attempt and why, with the change in whole requests it predicts, labelled a prediction; once a ready check has run, its `ready-verdict.json` and the measured change.
114|7. **Failure ledger,** kept by the lead: each graded attempt that lost, the size or phase it lost at, its named cause and its approach (`SKILL.md` step 4, *Harden*).
115|8. **Unverified:** what no one measured, the boundary's *can't see* list at least.
116|9. **Checks:** each checker's verdict, `pass` or its defects with file and line.
117|
118|## The checklist
119|
120|Fill it in for each piece of code you inspect, so that no piece is judged without its neighbours:
121|
122|- **Callers:** who calls it, and with what shapes at 1, 8 and 32 rows of a decode step and in a prefill.
123|- **Callees:** what it calls, down to the Metal kernel it launches.
124|- **Data:** each input and output with shape, dtype and layout. Where it is produced, and where it is consumed next.
125|- **Neighbours:** what runs just before and after it in the decode step, and what a replacement must keep identical.
126|- **Cost:** the kernels it launches, the bytes it reads and writes (weight bytes counted per read), and its measured time with the table the time comes from.
127|- **Invariants:** what correctness depends on: G2's bit-exact rule at every size, the tie rule for the 4th and 5th expert, the bfloat16 rounding points, and which MLX kernel the reference uses at each size.
128|
129|## The log
130|
131|Append one line per event with the shell, so lines from several agents never mix. In round 2:
132|
133|```bash
134|printf '%s | %s | %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "explorer-baseline-experts" "posted ineff-baseline-experts-2: each weight byte read 4 times at 32 rows" >> muse-spark/round-2/exploration/log.md
135|```
136|
137|Log when you start, claim something, post or confirm an entry, change direction (what from, what to, and which entry made you), grade an attempt (with its verdict), and finish.
138|
139|## Adapting to the others' work
140|
141|Before every new piece of work, and after every post:
142|1. Read the phase README's tracker and the newest 30 lines of the phase log (`tail -n 30`).
143|2. Then change direction when:
144|   - **someone else covers it:** another entry already covers the same code or cause, so append to that entry instead of starting a second one;
145|   - **its premise fell:** the claim your work rests on was refuted;
146|   - **something pays more:** an open item in your territory or task predicts a larger saving than what you're on, and nobody owns it.
147|3. When you change direction, log it with the reason, and write it in your own entry's status block.
148|
149|Two claims on the same item go to the lead, who settles them.
150|
151|## Rules for every agent
152|
153|- **Writes go only to this round's folder, in the files your role names.** Earlier rounds' folders, everything else in the worktree, and everything outside it are read-only.
154|- **Only the lead commits.** Helpers never run `git add` or `git commit`.
155|- **The grader and the ready check are the only GPU jobs.** Builders run the grader through the brief's command; the lead runs the ready check (`SKILL.md` step 4). Both wait their turn for the GPU. Start no other GPU work and load no model outside them: the machine has 16 GB and slows down sharply when memory runs short. A run of `time_candidates.py`, `breakdown.py` or any other timing script made directly is evidence of nothing.
156|- **Every number has a source,** and every speed number says its level and its kind:
157|  - **measured, piece:** the grader verdict that timed exactly that slot, `grade.json` in its attempt folder;
158|  - **measured, whole request:** the `ready-verdict.json` that timed exactly that slot or combination;
159|  - **prediction:** anything else. It counts only the candidate's own measured effect, shows its arithmetic, and stands beside the measured value once there is one.
160|
161|  A combination is measured as one, never added up from its slots. What no one measured goes under **Unverified**, never assumed free, neutral or zero. Other numbers cite a file and line, a table (path and row), or arithmetic shown in full.
162|- **Credentials stay unread:** `.env` files, `~/.config/muse/` and any key store.
163|- **The API-stage kernels** in the history before the tag `agent-era` are from an earlier, removed stage (PROVENANCE.md) and stay unread.
